words.tr:
v. 行动；表现；演戏；
n. 行动；法令；
words.ex: He acted quickly to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速行动救了那个孩子。
words.en: To do something for a particular purpose or in a particular way; to behave in a particular way; to have an effect or influence on something; to perform a part in a play, film, etc.

words.ex: The government took quick action to fix the problem.
words.ex_cn: 政府迅速采取行动解决问题。
words.en: The fact or process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim.

words.tr: adj. 活跃的；积极的；主动的；
words.ex: He is an active student in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上是一个活跃的学生。
words.en: Someone who is active moves around a lot or does a lot of things.

words.ex: The school organized a fun activity for the students.
words.ex_cn: 学校为学生们组织了一场有趣的活动。
words.en: An activity is something that you spend time doing.

words.ex: He is an actor in a famous movie.
words.ex_cn: 他是电影中的一名演员。
words.en: An actor is a person whose profession is acting on the stage, in films, or on television.

words.ex: The actress sings in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位女演员在电影中唱歌。
words.en: An actress is a woman whose profession is acting on the stage, in films, or on television.

words.ex: The prince rode a white horse through the castle gate.
words.ex_cn: 王子骑着一匹白马穿过城堡的大门。
words.en: A prince is a male member of a royal family, especially the son of a king or queen.

words.ex: The princess lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 公主住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A princess is a female member of a royal family, especially a daughter or granddaughter of a king and queen, or the wife of a prince.

words.ex: The actual cost was lower than expected.
words.ex_cn: 实际成本比预期的低。
words.en: You use actual to emphasize that you are referring to something real or genuine.

words.tr: adv. 事实上；实际上；竟然；
words.ex: I thought he was late, but actually he was on time.
words.ex_cn: 我以为他迟到了，但事实上他准时到了。
words.en: You use actually to indicate that a situation exists or happened, or to emphasize that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: He is virtually always on time.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是准时。
words.en: In effect though not formally recognized; practically.

words.ex: He reacts quickly when he hears a loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到大声响时，他会迅速做出反应。
words.en: When you react to something that has happened to you, you behave in a particular way because of it.

words.ex: His reaction was quick when the ball came at him.
words.ex_cn: 当球朝他飞来时，他的反应很快。
words.en: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.

words.ex: He gave the exact time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了会议的确切时间。
words.en: If you describe something as exact, you mean that it is precise and accurate in all its details.

words.tr: adv. 确切地；正是；准确地；
words.ex: He arrived exactly at 8 o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 他正好在八点到达。
words.en: In a precise manner; accurately.

words.ex: He adds two and three to get five.
words.ex_cn: 他把二和三相加得到五。
words.en: To put something together with something else so as to increase the size, number, or amount.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: He needs additional time to finish the homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要额外的时间来完成作业。
words.en: If something is additional, it is extra and is added to what is already there.

words.ex: He likes apples. In addition, he likes oranges.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果。另外，他喜欢橙子。
words.en: You use in addition when you want to mention another item connected with the subject you are discussing.

words.tr:
adj. 相等的；同等的；
v. 等于；比得上；
words.ex: Two plus two is equal to four.
words.ex_cn: 二加二等于四。
words.en: If two things are equal, or if one thing is equal to another, they are the same in size, number, standard, or value.

words.ex: Everyone deserves equality in education.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都应享有教育平等。
words.en: Equality is the state of being equal, especially in status, rights, or opportunities.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: I admire my teacher for her patience.
words.ex_cn: 我钦佩我的老师有耐心。
words.en: If you admire someone or something, you like and respect them very much.

words.ex: Her courage in facing danger is admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在面对危险时表现出的勇气令人钦佩。
words.en: If you say that something is admirable, you mean that you approve of it or respect it.

words.ex: She adores her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她非常喜爱她的弟弟。
words.en: If you adore someone, you feel great love and admiration for them.

words.tr: adj. 可爱的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The puppy is adorable.
words.ex_cn: 这只小狗很可爱。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is adorable, you are emphasizing that they are very attractive and you feel great affection for them.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: He wants to publish a book next year.
words.ex_cn: 他想明年出版一本书。
words.en: To produce and issue printed material for public distribution or sale; to make information or work available to the public.

words.ex: The teacher will punish the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师会因为作弊而惩罚那个学生。
words.en: To punish someone means to make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 发展；进步；提前；
adj. 预先的；在前的；
v. 前进；发展；提前；
words.ex: The advance of technology has changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展改变了我们的生活。
words.en: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help it to succeed.

words.tr: adj. 先进的；高级的； v. 提前；前进；“advance”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This school uses advanced technology in classrooms.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校在教室里使用先进的技术。
words.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: The disadvantage of living far away is long commute time.
words.ex_cn: 住得远的劣势是通勤时间长。
words.en: A disadvantage is a factor which makes someone or something less useful, acceptable, or successful than other people or things.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: The company will advertise its new phone on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司将在电视上为新手机登广告。
words.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

words.ex: He saw an advertisement on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他在电视上看到一则广告。
words.en: An advertisement is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event or publicizing a job vacancy.

words.ex: The soldier was spying on the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 这名士兵在夜间秘密侦察敌军营地。
words.en: A spy is a person who secretly collects and reports information about the activities, movements, and plans of an enemy or competitor.

words.ex: One aspect of learning English is practicing speaking.
words.ex_cn: 学习英语的一个方面是练习口语。
words.en: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

words.tr:
n. 旋转；
v. 旋转；
words.ex: The spin of the top made it stay upright.
words.ex_cn: 陀螺的旋转让它保持直立。
words.en: If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.

words.tr:
n. 方面；尊重；尊敬；
v. 遵从；尊重；尊敬；
words.ex: In this respect, the plan is good.
words.ex_cn: 在这个方面，这个计划很好。
words.en: If you respect someone, you have a good opinion of their character or ideas.

words.ex: The prospect of a better job makes him happy.
words.ex_cn: 更好工作的前景让他感到高兴。
words.en: A prospect is the possibility that something will happen, or a view of a wide area.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The teacher will inspect our homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会检查我们的作业。
words.en: If you inspect something, you look at it very carefully, usually in order to find out something about it.

words.tr: n. 检查；视察；查看；审视；
words.ex: The teacher did an inspection of the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师对教室进行了检查。
words.en: An inspection is an official visit to a building or organization to check that everything is satisfactory and that rules are being obeyed.

words.ex: I expect a gift on my birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我期待在生日时收到一份礼物。
words.en: If you expect something, you believe that it is likely to happen or that it will be the case.

words.tr: adj. 想不到的；意料之外的；
words.ex: The rain was unexpected.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨是意想不到的。
words.en: If an event or someone's behaviour is unexpected, it surprises you because you were not expecting it to happen or because you did not think that person would behave in that way.

words.ex: His expectation was to pass the test.
words.ex_cn: 他的期待是通过考试。
words.en: An expectation is a belief about what might happen in the future, especially about something that you think is likely or that you hope will happen.

words.ex: The spectator watched the game quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地观看了比赛。
words.en: A spectator is someone who watches an event, show, game, or activity.

words.ex: The audience clapped loudly after the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
words.en: The group of spectators at a public event; listeners or viewers collectively, especially those attending a performance or reading a particular work.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: His guess about the winner was just speculation.
words.ex_cn: 他对获胜者的猜测只是推测。
words.en: The act of forming opinions about what has happened or what might happen without knowing all the facts.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.ex: I suspect it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我猜想明天会下雨。
words.en: If you suspect someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you believe that they have done it, although you have no proof.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.tr: adj. 怀疑的；令人怀疑的；
words.ex: The police felt suspicious about the man's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 警察对这个人的行为感到怀疑。
words.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you do not trust them, and are careful when dealing with them.

words.ex: The painter used vivid colors to show the forest.
words.ex_cn: 画家用鲜艳的颜色来描绘森林。
words.en: If you describe memories and descriptions as vivid, you mean that they are very clear and detailed.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.tr: v. 幸存；生存；存活；艰难挺过；
words.ex: He survived the accident with minor injuries.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中幸存下来，只有轻微受伤。
words.en: If you survive in a dangerous situation, you continue to live or exist in spite of it.

words.ex: The survivor walked out of the forest after three days.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者在三天后走出了森林。
words.en: A survivor is someone who continues to live after an event in which others have died, or someone who manages to continue living their life successfully despite difficulties.

words.ex: The survival of the animals depends on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物的生存取决于天气。
words.en: The state or fact of continuing to live or exist, typically in spite of an accident, ordeal, or difficult circumstances.

words.tr:
n. 表面；
v. 显露；
words.ex: The surface of the table is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的表面很光滑。
words.en: The outer or top part of something; to rise to the surface of water or to become known after being hidden or secret.

words.ex: He wiped the table with a cloth.
words.ex_cn: 他用一块布擦了桌子。
words.en: To wipe something means to clean or dry it by rubbing its surface with a cloth, a piece of paper, or your hand.

words.ex: She sweeps the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上扫地。
words.en: To clean an area by brushing away dirt or litter.

words.tr:
n. 杂草；野草；
v. 除草；铲除；
words.ex: The garden is full of weeds.
words.ex_cn: 花园里长满了杂草。
words.en: A weed is a wild plant that grows in gardens or fields of crops and is not wanted because it harms the plants that are being grown.

words.ex: The cat hid behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 猫躲到了灌木丛后面。
words.en: A bush is a plant which is much smaller than a tree and has a lot of branches.

words.ex: He has a bushy beard.
words.ex_cn: 他有一把浓密的胡须。
words.en: If something is bushy, it has a lot of leaves or branches growing close together.

words.tr:
n. 刷子；灌木丛；
v. 刷；
words.ex: He cleaned the floor with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子打扫了地板。
words.en: A brush is an object with a handle and a large number of bristles, hairs, or wires fixed to it, used for cleaning, painting, or arranging hair.

words.ex: The artist's brushwork is distinctive and bold.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的笔法独特而大胆。
words.en: Brushwork refers to the particular way in which an artist applies paint with a brush.

words.ex: The lion lives in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在丛林中。
words.en: A jungle is a dense, tropical forest that is home to a wide variety of plants and animals.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.ex: He swore he didn't steal the money.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓他没有偷钱。
words.en: If someone swears, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, usually because they are angry.

words.tr:
v. 传播；扩散；散布；
n. 传播；蔓延；范围；
words.ex: The virus spread quickly through the city.
words.ex_cn: 病毒在城市中迅速传播。
words.en: To spread something means to open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

words.tr: adj. 流传甚广的；分布广的；
words.ex: The flu became widespread last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感流传甚广。
words.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

words.ex: The bird spread its wing to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟张开翅膀飞翔。
words.en: One of the two flat parts that stick out from the side of a bird's body and are used for flying.

words.tr:
n. 摇摆；
v. 摇摆；
words.ex: The child enjoyed the swing at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子喜欢在公园里荡秋千。
words.en: If something swings or if you swing it, it moves repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side from a fixed point. If you swing somewhere, you move there by holding onto something and moving your body through the air.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动
n. 摇摆；爱说笑的人
words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: If a dog wags its tail, it moves its tail from side to side, often because it is happy or excited.

words.tr:
v. 转换；
n. 开关；
words.ex: He switched off the light before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前把灯关掉了。
words.en: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

words.ex: The witch flew on a broomstick at night.
words.ex_cn: 巫婆在夜里骑着扫帚飞行。
words.en: A woman who is believed to have magical powers and who uses them to harm or help other people.

words.tr:
v. 交换；
n. 交换；
words.ex: They swap books every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周交换书籍。
words.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

words.tr:
n. 交换；兑换；交易所；
v. 交换；
words.ex: They made an exchange of books.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了书籍的交换。
words.en: If you exchange something, you give it to someone and receive something else in return.

words.ex: The dove is a symbol of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: A symbol is a shape or design that is used to represent something such as an idea, a quality, or a process.

words.ex: The dove is a symbolic bird of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征性鸟类。
words.en: If you describe an event, action, or procedure as symbolic, you mean that it represents an important change, although it has little practical effect.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: He listened to a beautiful symphony last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚听了一首美妙的交响乐。
words.en: A symphony is a long piece of music that is usually in four parts and is performed by an orchestra.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: The boat was at the mercy of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船听任风暴摆布。
words.en: If one person or thing is at the mercy of another, the first person or thing is in a situation where they cannot prevent themselves being harmed or affected by the second.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈悲的；宽大的
words.ex: The judge was merciful and gave him a small fine.
words.ex_cn: 法官很仁慈，只判了他一笔小额罚款。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as merciful, you mean that they show or have mercy.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.tr: v. 遗弃；抛弃；“abandon”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 被遗弃了的；
words.ex: They abandoned the old car by the road.
words.ex_cn: 他们把那辆旧车遗弃在路边。
words.en: Left behind or deserted; given up.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: She decided to have an abortion.
words.ex_cn: 她决定进行流产。
words.en: An abortion is a medical procedure to end a pregnancy so it does not result in the birth of a baby.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: He gave her an abusive shout.
words.ex_cn: 他对她大喊大叫，态度虐待。
words.en: If someone is abusive, they use rude and insulting words or behave violently towards someone else.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.ex: His temperature is normal.
words.ex_cn: 他的体温正常。
words.en: Something that is normal is usual and ordinary, and is what people expect.

words.ex: He normally goes to bed at 10 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 他通常晚上10点睡觉。
words.en: If you say that something normally happens or that you normally do a particular thing, you mean that it is what usually happens or what you usually do.

words.tr:
n. 标准；
adj. 标准的；规范的；
words.ex: The school has a high standard for homework.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校对作业有很高的标准。
words.en: A standard is a level of quality or achievement, especially a level that is thought to be acceptable.

words.tr: n. 风格；方式；样式；文体；
words.ex: Her dress has a unique style.
words.ex_cn: 她的裙子有一种独特的风格。
words.en: A particular kind, sort, or type, as with reference to form, appearance, or character.

words.ex: She wears stylish clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着时髦的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is stylish is fashionable and attractive.

words.tr:
n. 类型；种类；典型；字体；
v. 打字；
words.ex: This is a new type of phone.
words.ex_cn: 这是一种新型手机。
words.en: A type is a category of things or people that have similar characteristics.

words.ex: She is a fast typist.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位打字很快的打字员。
words.en: A typist is someone who types, especially as their job.

words.ex: He typed the letter on an old typewriter.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台旧打字机打了这封信。
words.en: A typewriter is a machine with keys that you press to print letters, numbers, or other characters onto paper.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.ex: She typically arrives early for class.
words.ex_cn: 她往往很早就到课。
words.en: You use typically to say that something usually happens in the way that you are describing.

words.ex: He was absent from school yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天缺席了学校。
words.en: If someone or something is absent from a place or situation where they should be or where they usually are, they are not there.

words.ex: His absence of interest made the teacher sad.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习的缺乏兴趣让老师感到难过。
words.en: The state of being away from a place or person.

words.tr:
adj. 目前的；在场的；
n. 目前；礼物；
v. 呈现；提出；
words.ex: The present situation is very difficult.
words.ex_cn: 目前的形势非常困难。
words.en: If you say that someone is present at an event, you mean that they are there.

words.ex: His presence made everyone feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他的存在让每个人都感到平静。
words.en: The state or fact of existing, occurring, or being present in a place or thing.

words.ex: He gave a presentation about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个关于气候变化的报告。
words.en: The act of showing or explaining something to an audience.

words.tr: v. 代表；表现；体现；相当于；
words.ex: He represents his country in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中代表他的国家。
words.en: If someone represents a person or group of people, they act on behalf of that person or group.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful representation of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是对自然的美丽表现。
words.en: A representation of something is a picture, a model of it, or a description of it that you create or that someone else creates for you.

words.tr:
n. 代表；典型事物；
adj. 典型的；有代表性的；代议制的；
words.ex: He is the representative of our class.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们班的代表。
words.en: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

words.ex: He spoke on behalf of his team.
words.ex_cn: 他代表他的团队发言。
words.en: If you do something on someone's behalf, you do it for that person as their representative.

words.ex: The child behaves well in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现得很好。
words.en: To behave means to act in a particular way, especially in a way that is good or correct.

words.ex: His behaviour at school is very good.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校的行为很好。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.ex: She gave him a gift for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 她送了他一份生日礼物。
words.en: A gift is something that you give someone as a present. It can also refer to a natural ability or talent.

words.tr: adj. 有才华的；有天赋的；
words.ex: He is a gifted musician who plays piano beautifully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有才华的音乐家，钢琴弹得非常优美。
words.en: Having a natural ability or talent.

words.ex: He put the letter in an envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把信装进了一个信封。
words.en: An envelope is a flat, usually rectangular or square, paper container for a letter, which you seal before you send it by post.

words.tr: adj. 能够；能…的；有能力的；
words.ex: He is able to swim across the river.
words.ex_cn: 他能够游过这条河。
words.en: If you are able to do something, you have the skills, strength, knowledge, or other qualities needed to do it.

words.ex: He is unable to swim.
words.ex_cn: 他不会游泳。
words.en: If you are unable to do something, you cannot do it, either because you do not have the necessary skill or knowledge, or because you do not have the opportunity to do it.

words.ex: The accident disabled him for life.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他终身残废。
words.en: If an injury or illness disables someone, it affects them so badly that it restricts the way that they can live their life.

words.tr: n. 伤残；失去能力；无能力；
words.ex: He has a disability that makes walking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 他有伤残，导致行走困难。
words.en: A disability is a physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements, senses, or activities.

words.tr: adj. 残疾的； v. “disable”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The disabled man uses a wheelchair to move around.
words.ex_cn: 这位残疾人使用轮椅行动。
words.en: If someone is disabled, they are unable to use part of their body or mind properly, for example, because of injury or illness.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: He showed great capability in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题上展现了很强的能力。
words.en: The ability or qualities necessary to do something.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

words.tr:
v. 逃避；逃走；
n. 逃脱；逃避；
words.ex: He tried to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃离监狱。
words.en: To escape means to get away from a place or a situation that you are in, especially because it is difficult or dangerous to stay there.

words.tr:
n. 首都；财富；大写字母；
adj. 大写的；
words.ex: Beijing is the capital of China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的首都。
words.en: The city or town that functions as the seat of government and administrative center of a country or region.

words.ex: He capitalised on the chance to travel abroad.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了去国外旅行的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to take advantage of a particular opportunity or to write a letter or word in capital letters. It can also refer to providing a company with the money it needs to function.

words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.tr:
n. 插图说明；标题；字幕
v. 加上说明；加上标题；加上字幕
words.ex: The photo has a caption that says 'Happy birthday'.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片有一个标题，写着‘生日快乐’。
words.en: A caption is a short piece of text under a picture in a book, magazine, or newspaper that describes the picture or explains what is happening in it.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

words.tr:
n. 污点；
v. 玷污；
words.ex: There is a coffee stain on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一个咖啡污点。
words.en: A stain is a mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid such as blood or coffee. To stain something means to leave a mark on it that is difficult to remove.

words.ex: He obtained a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周获得了一份新工作。
words.en: If you obtain something, you get it or achieve it.

words.tr: adj. 能获得的；可得到的
words.ex: The prize is obtainable if you win the game.
words.ex_cn: 如果你赢了比赛，这个奖品就能得到。
words.en: If something is obtainable, it is possible to get it.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: His attainment of the goal took many years.
words.ex_cn: 他达到这个目标花了多年时间。
words.en: The act of achieving something, especially through effort; a skill or accomplishment that has been achieved.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: The city plans for sustainability by using solar energy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过使用太阳能来实现可持续性。
words.en: Sustainability is the ability to maintain or support a process continuously over time. In the context of environmental science, it refers to the avoidance of the depletion of natural resources in order to maintain an ecological balance.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.ex: She put the apples in a plastic container.
words.ex_cn: 她把苹果放进了一个塑料容器里。
words.en: A container is something such as a box or bottle that is used to hold or store things in.

words.tr: v. 保持；维护；坚持认为；供养；
words.ex: He tries to maintain a healthy diet.
words.ex_cn: 他努力保持健康的饮食。
words.en: To keep something in existence or continue to provide support for it, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: He will fix the broken chair tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修理那把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: To fix something means to repair it, to make it firm or stable, or to arrange or decide it.

words.ex: The temperature remains high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天温度保持很高。
words.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.

words.ex: The main reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The most important part or aspect of something.

words.ex: He mainly eats vegetables and fruit.
words.ex_cn: 他主要吃蔬菜和水果。
words.en: You use mainly to indicate that a statement is true in most cases or to a large extent.

words.tr:
adj. 男性的；雄性的；
n. 男性；雄性；
words.ex: The male bird has bright red feathers.
words.ex_cn: 这只雄鸟有鲜艳的红色羽毛。
words.en: A male is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that cannot have babies. In humans, males are usually considered to be boys or men.

words.tr:
adj. 女性的；雌性的；
n. 雌性；女性；
words.ex: The female teacher is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 这位女老师非常和蔼。
words.en: A female is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that can have babies or produce eggs.

words.ex: That guy is waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 那个家伙正在等公交车。
words.en: A guy is a man or boy. You can refer to a group of people, especially men or boys, as guys.

words.tr:
n. 同事；（组织的）会员；家伙；同胞；
adj. 同类的；同事的；
words.ex: He works as a fellow with Dr. Smith in the lab.
words.ex_cn: 他在实验室里与史密斯博士一起工作，是他的同事。
words.en: A fellow is a man or boy. In British English, a fellow is also a member of certain academic societies.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.tr: adj. 接着的；下列的； prep. 在...之后； v. 跟随；“follow”的现在分词； n. 下列各项；
words.ex: The following day, we went to the park.
words.ex_cn: 接着的那天，我们去了公园。
words.en: Coming after or as a result of something; a group of supporters or admirers.

words.ex: The new tool enables him to finish work faster.
words.ex_cn: 这个新工具使他能够更快地完成工作。
words.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity or means to do it.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.tr: phrase. v. 详述；扩述；进一步说明
words.ex: He will enlarge on the idea in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他将在演讲中详细阐述这个想法。
words.en: To add more details or information to a statement, story, or explanation. (A variant spelling of 'enlarge upon'.)

words.ex: His strength helped him lift the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他的力量让他举起了那个重箱子。
words.en: The quality or state of being physically strong.

words.ex: Exercise can strengthen your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To strengthen something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: The length of the table is two meters.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的长度是两米。
words.en: The measurement or extent of something from end to end; the greater of two or the greatest of three dimensions of a body.

words.ex: He talked at length about his trip finally.
words.ex_cn: 他最后详细谈到了他的旅行。
words.en: If someone does something at length, they do it for a long time or in great detail.

words.ex: She will lengthen the dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她会把裙子改长一点去参加派对。
words.en: To make something longer, or to become longer.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.ex: He will fasten his seatbelt before driving.
words.ex_cn: 他开车前会系好安全带。
words.en: To close or attach something firmly so that it will not open or come loose.

words.ex: The lid is tight on the jar.
words.ex_cn: 罐子的盖子很紧。
words.en: Something that is tight is fastened or fixed firmly and is not loose.

words.ex: He tightened the screw with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 他用扳手把螺丝拧紧。
words.en: If you tighten a rule, policy, or system, you make it stricter or more efficient.

words.tr: adj. 未固定牢的；宽松的；
words.ex: The loose screw fell off the table.
words.ex_cn: 那个松动的螺丝从桌子上掉了下来。
words.en: Not firmly or tightly fixed in place; detached or able to be detached.

words.ex: He lost his keys yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天丢了钥匙。
words.en: If you lose something, you no longer have it or you cannot find it.

words.tr: adj. 丢失的； v. 丢失；输；“lose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The lost keys were found under the table.
words.ex_cn: 丢失的钥匙在桌子下面找到了。
words.en: If you are lost, you do not know where you are or you are unable to find your way.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.ex: The company suffered a big loss last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年遭受了巨大损失。
words.en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than you used to have, or the process by which this happens.

words.ex: The loud noise frightened the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something or someone frightens you, they cause you to suddenly feel afraid, anxious, or nervous.

words.tr:
v. 打架；战斗；
n. 打架；战斗；
words.ex: The two boys fight every day after school.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天放学后都打架。
words.en: To fight means to take part in a violent struggle involving the exchange of physical blows or the use of weapons. It can also refer to a determined effort to achieve or resist something.

words.tr: adj. 惊吓的；受惊的；害怕的； v. “frighten”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was frightened by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 孩子被巨大的噪音吓到了。
words.en: If you are frightened, you are anxious or afraid, often because of something that has just happened or that you think may happen.

words.ex: The loud noise scared the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

words.ex: The conflict between the two countries lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家之间的冲突持续了多年。
words.en: A conflict is a serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

words.ex: The movie caused a feeling of terror in the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众感到恐怖。
words.en: Terror is a very strong feeling of fear, especially fear that you experience suddenly.

words.ex: The police caught the terrorist near the station.
words.ex_cn: 警察在车站附近抓住了这名恐怖分子。
words.en: A terrorist is a person who uses violent and intimidating methods in the pursuit of political aims.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.tr: adj. 可怕的；极坏的；糟糕的；
words.ex: The storm caused a terrible flood.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了一场可怕的洪水。
words.en: If something is terrible, it is very bad or of very poor quality.

words.ex: The movie was horrible and made me scared.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很恐怖，让我害怕。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as horrible, you mean they are very unpleasant or bad.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: The storm is a threat to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对村庄构成了威胁。
words.en: A threat is a statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage, or other hostile action on someone in retribution for something done or not done.

words.ex: He throw the ball to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他把球扔给他的朋友。
words.en: To propel something through the air with a movement of the arm and hand.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.ex: He had a sore throat after singing all night.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一整晚后喉咙疼。
words.en: Your throat is the back part of your mouth, where it connects to your neck. It includes the passage that leads from your mouth to your stomach and lungs.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The volume of the box is 10 cubic meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的体积是10立方米。
words.en: A volume is a book, especially one that is part of a series of books. It can also refer to the amount of space that a substance or object occupies, or the level of sound produced by a television, radio, etc.

words.tr:
n. 板；董事会；
v. 上船（或火车、飞机等）；
words.ex: He nailed the picture to the board.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片钉在板上。
words.en: A board is a flat, thin, rectangular piece of wood or other material used for a particular purpose, such as cutting food on or as a surface for writing or playing games. It can also refer to a group of people who manage or control a company or organization, or to the meals provided by an institution such as a school or hospital. As a verb, it means to get onto a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle, or to provide meals and lodging for someone.

words.ex: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
words.ex_cn: 老师在黑板上写字。
words.en: A blackboard is a dark-colored board that you can write on with chalk, used especially in classrooms.

words.ex: She put the plates in the cupboard.
words.ex_cn: 她把盘子放在碗橱里。
words.en: A cupboard is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves that is used for storing things, usually in a kitchen.

words.ex: The passengers are aboard the plane.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在飞机上。
words.en: On or onto a ship, aircraft, bus, or train.

words.ex: The river is broad and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这条河宽阔而平缓。
words.en: Something that is broad is wide.

words.ex: He went abroad to study medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他去国外学医。
words.en: In or to a foreign country or countries.

words.tr:
adj. 广泛的；宽的；宽阔的；
adv. 广大地；
words.ex: The book has wide use in schools.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在学校里被广泛使用。
words.en: Something that is wide measures a large distance from one side to the other.

words.ex: This book is widely used in schools.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在学校里被广泛使用。
words.en: In a way that extends over a large area or range; extensively.

words.tr:
adv. 全球性地；
adj. 全球性的；
words.ex: The news spread worldwide overnight.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻一夜之间传遍全球。
words.en: Something that is worldwide exists or happens in all parts of the world.

words.tr: adj. 野生的；狂热的；荒芜的；猛烈的；
words.ex: The lion is a wild animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种野生动物。
words.en: Living or growing in the natural environment; not domesticated or cultivated.

words.ex: The wildness of the forest surprised her.
words.ex_cn: 森林的荒野让她感到惊讶。
words.en: The state or quality of being wild, uncultivated, or untamed.

words.ex: The park protects many kinds of wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园保护许多种类的野生生物。
words.en: Wildlife refers to animals and plants that live and grow in natural conditions.

words.tr:
n. 广播节目；电视节目；
v. 广播；播送；
words.ex: I listened to the morning broadcast on the radio.
words.ex_cn: 我听了早上的广播节目。
words.en: To broadcast is to transmit (a program or some information) by radio or television.

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.ex: The king lives in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 国王住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A castle is a large building or group of buildings fortified against attack with thick walls, battlements, towers, and in many cases a moat.

words.ex: The king lives in a big palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王住在一座巨大的宫殿里。
words.en: A palace is a very large impressive house, especially one which is the official home of a king, queen, or president.

words.ex: He cheated on the test by copying answers.
words.ex_cn: 他通过抄答案来作弊。
words.en: To cheat means to act dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage, especially in a game or examination.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.ex: I receive a letter from my friend every week.
words.ex_cn: 我每周都收到朋友的一封信。
words.en: To get or be given something; to welcome someone officially or socially.

words.ex: He picked up the receiver to answer the phone.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起听筒接电话。
words.en: A receiver is a person who receives something or a device that receives signals and converts them into sound or pictures.

words.ex: He kept the receipt for his new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了新鞋的收据。
words.en: A receipt is a piece of paper that you get from someone as proof that they have received money or goods from you.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.ex: The receptionist greeted the visitors with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 接待员微笑着迎接了访客。
words.en: A receptionist is a person whose job is to deal with people arriving at or telephoning a hotel, office building, doctor's surgery, etc.

words.ex: He accepted the gift with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着接受了这份礼物。
words.en: If you accept something that you have been offered, you say yes to it or agree to take it.

words.ex: The concept of freedom is important in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 自由这个观念在许多国家都很重要。
words.en: A concept is an idea or abstract principle.

words.ex: The teacher explained the conceptual meaning of gravity.
words.ex_cn: 老师解释了重力的概念含义。
words.en: Relating to or based on mental concepts.

words.ex: The sponge absorbs water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 海绵很快吸收水。
words.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

words.tr: phrase. 全神贯注于；专心于
words.ex: He is absorbed in reading a book.
words.ex_cn: 他正专心致志地读书。
words.en: To be so interested in something that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.ex: He worked hard and succeeded in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，考试成功了。
words.en: To achieve something that you have been aiming for, or to take over a position or role after someone else.

words.ex: Her hard work led to success.
words.ex_cn: 她的努力带来了成功。
words.en: The achievement of something desired, planned, or attempted.

words.ex: He is a successful businessman.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成功的商人。
words.en: Achieving the results wanted or hoped for.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: Graduating with honors was her greatest accomplishment.
words.ex_cn: 以优异成绩毕业是她最大的成就。
words.en: Something that has been achieved successfully.

words.tr: v. 完成；实现；达到；获得；
words.ex: He worked hard to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以完成他的目标。
words.en: To achieve something means to reach a particular goal or result through effort, skill, or courage.

words.ex: He felt proud of his academic achievement.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的学业成就感到自豪。
words.en: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: After the break, we will proceed with the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 休息后，我们将继续开会。
words.en: If you proceed to do something, you continue to do it or start to do it after doing something else first.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.ex: The troop marched into the town at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 部队在黎明时分进入城镇。
words.en: A troop is a group of soldiers or a large group of people or animals.

words.ex: My birthday is in March.
words.ex_cn: 我的生日在三月。
words.en: March is the third month of the Gregorian calendar, following February and preceding April.

words.ex: Follow the procedure step by step.
words.ex_cn: 一步一步地按照步骤进行。
words.en: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.ex: The computer has a fast processor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的处理器。
words.en: A processor is a part of a computer that interprets and carries out instructions.

words.ex: My ancestor came from China a hundred years ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先一百年前来自中国。
words.en: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.ex: The plane began its descent at 10,000 feet.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在一万英尺高度开始下降。
words.en: The act of moving or falling downward.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人建造了金字塔。
words.en: Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

words.tr: n. 进展；进步；缓慢前进；稳步前进；
words.ex: The project shows slow progress.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目进展缓慢。
words.en: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: Prior to the meeting, we reviewed the report.
words.ex_cn: 在会议之前，我们复习了报告。
words.en: Existing or coming before in time, order, or importance.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；问题；困难；
v. 费神；
words.ex: He got into trouble for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规则而惹上了麻烦。
words.en: If you say that someone is in trouble, you mean that they are in a situation that is difficult to deal with and that may cause them problems.

words.tr:
v. 陷入（困境）；设圈套；
n. 圈套；陷阱；困境；
words.ex: He trapped himself in debt by spending too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因花钱太多而陷入债务困境。
words.en: A trap is a device or enclosure designed to catch and retain animals, typically by allowing entry but not exit or by catching hold of a part of the body.

words.ex: He fastened the strap around his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他把带子系在手腕上。
words.en: A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material that is used to fasten, secure, or carry something, or to hold onto something.

words.ex: The factory uses a belt to move boxes.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用传送带来运送箱子。
words.en: A belt is a strip of leather or other material worn around the waist to support clothes or for decoration.

words.ex: He tied the box with a strong rope.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根结实的绳子把箱子绑了起来。
words.en: A rope is a thick cord made by twisting together strands of natural fibers such as hemp or artificial fibers such as nylon.

words.ex: The bike has a metal chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆自行车有一条金属链条。
words.en: A chain consists of connected links which are typically made of metal, used for fastening or securing something, or for transmitting mechanical power.

words.ex: He sat on the chair and read a book.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在椅子上读书。
words.en: A chair is a piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a back and usually four legs.

words.ex: She tied the box with a thin string.
words.ex_cn: 她用一根细线把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A string is a thin piece of rope or cord, or a series of things connected together.

words.tr:
n. 长条；条状；
v. 剥去；剥夺；
words.ex: He cut a strip of paper to wrap the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他剪了一条纸来包装礼物。
words.en: To remove a layer from something, or to take off your clothes.

words.ex: The tiger has black stripes on its orange fur.
words.ex_cn: 老虎的橙色皮毛上有黑色条纹。
words.en: A stripe is a long, narrow band or strip differing in color or texture from the surface on either side of it.

words.tr:
v. 计算；看作；清点；
n. 计数；计算；
words.ex: He counts the apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他计算桌子上的苹果数量。
words.en: To determine the total number of a collection of items.

words.ex: The kids are watching the countdown to New Year.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在观看新年的倒计时。
words.en: A countdown is the counting aloud of numbers in reverse order before something happens, especially before a spacecraft is launched.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.ex: He works as an accountant in a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司当会计师。
words.en: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep, inspect, and analyze financial accounts.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.ex: We work together every day.
words.ex_cn: 我们每天一起工作。
words.en: If people do something together, they do it with each other.

words.ex: There are altogether five apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上面总共有五个苹果。
words.en: Altogether is used to emphasize that something is completely the case or to indicate the total number or amount of something.

words.ex: He calculates the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算出总成本。
words.en: To determine by mathematical methods; compute.

words.ex: He uses a calculator to add numbers.
words.ex_cn: 他用计算器来加数字。
words.en: A calculator is a small electronic device that you use for doing mathematical calculations.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He sent an acknowledgement email after receiving the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他收到礼物后发了一封确认邮件。
words.en: An acknowledgement is a statement or action which recognizes that something exists or is true.

words.tr: n. 知识；了解；学问；学识；
words.ex: He gained knowledge from reading books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过读书获得了知识。
words.en: Knowledge is information and understanding about a subject which a person has, or which all people have.

words.ex: He is knowledgeable about history and science.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史和科学都很博学。
words.en: Someone who is knowledgeable has or shows a clear understanding of many different facts about the world or about a particular subject.

words.ex: I acquaint him with the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 我让他熟悉新规则。
words.en: If you acquaint someone with something, you tell them about it so that they know it.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.ex: I am familiar with this song.
words.ex_cn: 我熟悉这首歌。
words.en: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

words.ex: His familiarity with the city helped him find the way.
words.ex_cn: 他对这座城市的熟悉帮助他找到了路。
words.en: A thorough knowledge or mastery of a subject, place, or situation, often gained through experience.

words.ex: The teacher will familiarise students with basic math rules.
words.ex_cn: 老师将使学生熟悉基本的数学规则。
words.en: To make someone or yourself familiar with something; to learn about something so that you know it well.

words.ex: He wore a strange hat to school.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去学校。
words.en: If something is strange, it is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.

words.tr: n. 新来者；陌生人； adj. “strange”的比较级；
words.ex: He is a stranger in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个镇上的新来者。
words.en: A stranger is someone you have never met before.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: The oddness of his behavior made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他行为的古怪让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: The quality of being strange or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 常见的；普通的；共有的；
words.ex: Colds are a common illness in winter.
words.ex_cn: 感冒在冬天是很常见的疾病。
words.en: Something that is common happens often or is found in many places.

words.tr: adj. 通常的；寻常的；惯常的；
words.ex: He takes the usual bus to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通常坐这路公交车去上班。
words.en: If something is usual, it happens most often or was most often the case in the past.

words.tr: adj. 不平常的；不寻常的；
words.ex: It is unusual to see snow in this city.
words.ex_cn: 在这个城市看到雪是不平常的。
words.en: If something is unusual, it does not happen very often or you do not see it or hear it very often.

words.ex: She usually walks to school.
words.ex_cn: 她通常走路去学校。
words.en: Under normal conditions; generally.

words.tr:
n. 影响（力）；
v. 影响；
words.ex: The teacher had a big influence on her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生们有很大的影响。
words.en: The power to affect, control, or manipulate someone or something.

words.ex: He stayed home because he had the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他因为得了流感待在家里。
words.en: The flu is an infectious disease characterized by fever, aches and pains, and respiratory symptoms.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: Rain can affect the crop growth.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会影响作物生长。
words.en: To have an influence on or cause a change in someone or something.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 影响；作用；效果；效应；
words.ex: The new law had a big effect on traffic.
words.ex_cn: 新法律对交通产生了很大影响。
words.en: A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: The old machine is inefficient and uses too much energy.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器效率低，耗能太多。
words.en: If someone or something is inefficient, they do not use time, energy, or resources in the best way.

words.ex: He made a big effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他努力完成这个项目，按时交工。
words.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try hard to do it.

words.ex: She made the dance look effortless.
words.ex_cn: 她让舞蹈看起来毫不费力。
words.en: If you describe something as effortless, you mean that it is done or achieved with very little difficulty or work, often as a result of great skill.

words.ex: The recipe is perfect for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱对初学者来说是完备的。
words.en: Something that is perfect is as good as it could possibly be.

words.ex: She seeks perfection in everything she does.
words.ex_cn: 她在所做的每件事中都追求完美。
words.en: The state of being perfect; the highest degree of excellence or quality.

words.ex: The virus can infect people quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒能迅速感染人。
words.en: To infect someone or something means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.ex: The manufacturer makes cars in this factory.
words.ex_cn: 这家制造商在这家工厂生产汽车。
words.en: A manufacturer is a person or company that produces goods in large quantities, especially in a factory.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 诱导者；促进（或推动）…的事物
words.ex: The facilitator helped the group talk openly.
words.ex_cn: 诱导者帮助小组敞开心扉交谈。
words.en: A facilitator is a person or thing that makes an action or process easy or easier.

words.ex: The factory uses a big machine to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂用一台大机器制造汽车。
words.en: A machine is a piece of equipment which uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.

words.ex: The mechanic fixed my car quickly.
words.ex_cn: 机修工很快修好了我的车。
words.en: A mechanic is a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially those of vehicles.

words.ex: The mechanical toy moves with batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个机械玩具用电池驱动。
words.en: Relating to machines or machinery; operated by or involving a machine or machines.

words.ex: The factory makes cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂生产汽车。
words.en: A factory is a large building where machines are used to make goods in large quantities.

words.ex: We visited an art gallery on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们周日参观了一家艺术画廊。
words.en: A gallery is a place where works of art are shown to the public.

words.ex: He lives in the dormitory with three roommates.
words.ex_cn: 他和三个室友住在宿舍里。
words.en: A dormitory is a large bedroom where many people sleep, especially in a school or college.

words.ex: The children play at Nursery 796.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在796号托儿所玩耍。
words.en: A nursery is a place where young children are cared for during the day while their parents are at work.

words.tr: n. 护理（工作）；护理行业； v. “nurse”的现在分词；
words.ex: She works in nursing at the local hospital.
words.ex_cn: 她在当地医院从事护理工作。
words.en: The profession or practice of providing care for the sick and infirm.

words.ex: The students do experiments in the lab.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在实验室做实验。
words.en: A lab is a place where scientific experiments and research are conducted.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.ex: The mountain scenery is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 山景非常美丽。
words.en: The natural features of a landscape considered in terms of their appearance, especially when picturesque.

words.ex: The scene at the park was peaceful.
words.ex_cn: 公园里的场景很宁静。
words.en: A scene is a part of a play or film in which the action stays in one place for a continuous period of time.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.ex: The children played in the natural park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在自然公园里玩耍。
words.en: Existing in or caused by nature; not made or caused by humankind.

words.ex: He goes to the library every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午去图书馆。
words.en: A library is a building where books, documents, CDs, and sometimes videos and music are kept for people to read, study, or borrow.

words.ex: The librarian helps students find books.
words.ex_cn: 图书管理员帮助学生找书。
words.en: A librarian is a person who is in charge of a library or who has been trained to do this work.

words.ex: The lavatory is down the hall.
words.ex_cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
words.en: A lavatory is a room equipped with a toilet and sink for washing hands and face.

words.ex: The toilet is broken and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 马桶坏了，需要修理。
words.en: A toilet is a large bowl connected to the plumbing and used for urinating and defecating, typically fitted with a seat and flushing device.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.ex: Please remind me to call my mom tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 请提醒我明天给我妈妈打电话。
words.en: If someone reminds you of a fact or event that you already know about, they say something which makes you think about it.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.ex: The note on the fridge is a reminder to buy milk.
words.ex_cn: 冰箱上的便条是提醒买牛奶的东西。
words.en: A reminder is something that makes you think about or remember someone or something else.

words.ex: His memory is very good; he remembers everything.
words.ex_cn: 他的记忆力很好；他什么都记得。
words.en: Memory is the faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: He tries to memorise the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorise something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.tr: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；不朽作品；
words.ex: The ancient monument attracts many tourists each year.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代历史遗迹每年吸引许多游客。
words.en: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an important person or event.

words.ex: He buys milk and bread from the grocer.
words.ex_cn: 他从杂货店买牛奶和面包。
words.en: A grocer is a person who sells food and small household goods.

words.ex: He buys milk and bread at the grocery.
words.ex_cn: 他在杂货店买牛奶和面包。
words.en: A grocery is a store where food and small items for the house are sold.

words.tr: n. 果菜商；蔬菜水果店
words.ex: The greengrocer sells fresh apples and carrots.
words.ex_cn: 蔬果商贩出售新鲜的苹果和胡萝卜。
words.en: A greengrocer is a person who owns or works in a shop that sells fresh vegetables and fruit.

words.tr: n. 屠夫；肉贩； adj. “butch”的比较级；
words.ex: The butcher sold fresh meat at the market.
words.ex_cn: 屠夫在市场卖新鲜的肉。
words.en: A butcher is a person who prepares and sells meat. As a verb, to butcher means to kill and prepare animals for meat, or to kill people in a cruel and unnecessary way.

words.ex: The tailor made a new suit for the man.
words.ex_cn: 裁缝为这位男士做了一套新西装。
words.en: A tailor is a person whose job is to make men's clothes, especially suits, jackets, and trousers, that fit individual customers. As a verb, to tailor means to make or adapt something for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: The tail of an animal, bird, or fish is the part extending beyond the end of its body.

words.ex: He noticed every detail of the painting.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了这幅画的每一个细节。
words.en: A detail is a small individual feature or element of something.

words.ex: He works in retail at a small store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小店从事零售工作。
words.en: The sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.tr: adj. 详细的；细致的； v. “detail”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He gave a detailed description of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对事故做了详细的描述。
words.en: A detailed account or report contains a lot of details.

words.ex: The shopkeeper gave me a small discount.
words.ex_cn: 店主给了我一点折扣。
words.en: A shopkeeper is a person who owns or manages a shop.

words.ex: The retailer sells clothes to customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家零售商向顾客出售衣服。
words.en: A retailer is a person or business that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.tr:
adj. 批发的；
n. 成批出售；
adv. 大批地；
words.ex: He buys clothes at wholesale prices.
words.ex_cn: 他以批发价购买衣服。
words.en: Wholesale is the business of buying and selling goods in large quantities, especially for resale to retailers.

words.ex: The clerk at the store helped me find the book.
words.ex_cn: 商店里的职员帮我找到了那本书。
words.en: A clerk is a person whose job is to keep records or accounts in an office, shop, or bank.

words.tr: n. 代理人；特工；经纪人；（药）剂；动因；
words.ex: The real estate agent helped them buy a house.
words.ex_cn: 房地产代理人帮助他们买了一所房子。
words.en: An agent is a person who acts on behalf of another person or group.

words.ex: The agency helps people find jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这个机构帮助人们找工作。
words.en: An agency is a business which provides a service on behalf of other businesses.

words.ex: The doctor said the patient needs urgent care.
words.ex_cn: 医生说病人需要紧急治疗。
words.en: If something is urgent, it needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

words.ex: The doctor sensed the urgency and acted quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生感受到了紧急情况，迅速采取了行动。
words.en: The quality or condition of being urgent; pressing importance.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.tr:
n. 表；名单；
v. 列出；
words.ex: He wrote his name on the list.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己的名字写在了表上。
words.en: A list is a set of items, especially names, written or printed one after the other.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.tr: n. 含酒精的饮料；酒精；
words.ex: He drank alcohol at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上喝了含酒精的饮料。
words.en: Alcohol is a colourless liquid that can make you drunk, and which is used in medicines, cleaning products, and other substances.

words.ex: This drink is alcoholic and not for children.
words.ex_cn: 这种饮料含酒精，不适合儿童饮用。
words.en: An alcoholic is someone who cannot stop drinking large amounts of alcohol, even when it is causing them serious health or personal problems.

words.ex: He bought a cigarette at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了一支香烟。
words.en: A cigarette is a small roll of finely cut tobacco for smoking, enclosed in a wrapper of thin paper.

words.ex: He smokes tobacco every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吸烟草。
words.en: Tobacco is a plant that is grown for its leaves, which are dried and used for smoking in cigarettes, cigars, and pipes, or for chewing or snuffing.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.tr:
adj. 固体的；坚固的；可靠的；
n. 固体；
words.ex: Ice is a solid form of water.
words.ex_cn: 冰是水的固体形式。
words.en: A solid substance or object stays the same shape whether it is in a container or not.

words.ex: He put the lid on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他把盖子盖在盒子上。
words.en: A lid is a cover for a container, or the movable cover of the eye, known as the eyelid.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

words.tr:
v. 参观；访问；
n. 参观；访问；
words.ex: We visit the museum on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我们在周末参观博物馆。
words.en: To go to a place in order to look at it, or to a person in order to spend time with them.

words.ex: The visitor took photos of the museum.
words.ex_cn: 这位参观者拍了博物馆的照片。
words.en: A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

words.ex: The children learned through visual aids like pictures.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们通过图片等视觉辅助工具学习。
words.en: relating to seeing or to the eyes

words.ex: Try to visualise a red ball floating in the air.
words.ex_cn: 试着想象一个红色的球在空中漂浮。
words.en: To form a mental image of; imagine.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.ex: The chart is visually easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个图表在视觉上很容易理解。
words.en: In a way that relates to seeing or sight.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.ex: The teacher gave supervision to the students during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试期间监督学生。
words.en: The act of overseeing or directing a project, activity, or person.

words.ex: The supervisor checked the workers' progress.
words.ex_cn: 主管检查了工人们的进展。
words.en: A supervisor is a person who oversees and directs the work of others.

words.ex: She has excellent night vision.
words.ex_cn: 她有很好的夜视能力。
words.en: Vision is the ability to see, the area that you can see, the ability to imagine how a country, society, industry, etc. could develop in the future and to plan in a suitable way, or an experience in which you see something that is not really there.

words.tr: n. 电视节目；电视行业；电视机；
words.ex: He watches television every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上看电视节目。
words.en: A system for transmitting visual images and sound that are reproduced on screens, chiefly used to broadcast programs for entertainment, information, and education.

words.tr:
n. 见解；风景；视野；
v. 观看；审视；
words.ex: His view on education is very different from mine.
words.ex_cn: 他对教育的见解与我的非常不同。
words.en: Your view of a particular subject is the way that you understand and think about it.

words.ex: The viewer watched the movie on TV.
words.ex_cn: 观看者在电视上看了这部电影。
words.en: A viewer is someone who watches something, especially television.

words.ex: His viewpoint is different from mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的不同。
words.en: A viewpoint is a particular way of thinking about something, especially one that is influenced by your experiences or beliefs.

words.ex: He gave a quick preview of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他简要预看了这部电影。
words.en: A preview is an opportunity to see something such as a film or a collection of works of art before it is open to the public.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.tr:
n. 回顾；复习；审查；评论；
v. 回顾；复习；审核；评论；
words.ex: We had a quick review of last week's lesson.
words.ex_cn: 我们对上周的课程做了一个简短的回顾。
words.en: If you review something, you consider it again, especially in order to make changes to it or to give your opinion about it.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: He did revision for his math test last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚为数学考试进行了复习。
words.en: The act or process of revising; a revised or new version, as of a book or other written material.

words.ex: The journalist wrote a story about the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 记者写了一篇关于地震的文章。
words.en: A journalist is a person whose job is to collect news and write about it for newspapers, magazines, television, or radio.

words.ex: He reads a science journal every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周读一本科学期刊。
words.en: A journal is a newspaper or magazine that deals with a particular subject or professional activity.

words.ex: The reporter asked the president a difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 记者问了总统一个困难的问题。
words.en: A reporter is a person whose job is to discover information about news events and describe them for a newspaper, magazine, radio, or television.

words.ex: He reads a magazine every evening.
