words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.ex: The movie shows a fantasy, not reality.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示的是幻想，而不是现实。
words.en: Reality is the state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or might be imagined.

words.tr: v. 意识到；认识到；实现；
words.ex: He finally realised his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于意识到自己的错误。
words.en: To realise means to become fully aware of something as a fact; understand clearly. It also means to achieve something desired or anticipated.

words.tr:
v. 希望；
n. 希望；
words.ex: I hope it rains tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我希望明天下雨。
words.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

words.ex: The children are eager to open their presents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们渴望打开他们的礼物。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.ex: The eagle flies high above the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 鹰在山上面高飞。
words.en: A large bird of prey with a massive hooked bill and long broad wings, known for its keen sight and powerful soaring flight.

words.ex: I truly appreciate your help.
words.ex_cn: 我衷心感谢你的帮助。
words.en: You use truly to emphasize that something has all the features or qualities of a particular thing, or is the case to the fullest possible extent.

words.ex: The truth is that he was late for work.
words.ex_cn: 事实是他上班迟到了。
words.en: The truth is the true facts about something, rather than what is imagined or invented.

words.tr:
n. 曲调；调子；
v. 调整；调音；
words.ex: He hummed a happy tune while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时哼着一首欢快的曲调。
words.en: A tune is a series of musical notes that are pleasant to listen to. It can also refer to adjusting something so that it works or looks better.

words.ex: He speaks Chinese as his mother tongue.
words.ex_cn: 他把汉语作为母语。
words.en: The tongue is the flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used for tasting, licking, swallowing, and (in humans) articulating speech.

words.tr:
adj. 很好的；晴朗的；健康的；
n. 罚款；
words.ex: She did a fine job on the project.
words.ex_cn: 她在这个项目上做得很好。
words.en: If you say that something is fine, you mean that it is satisfactory or acceptable.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.ex: The teacher define the word 'love' in simple terms.
words.ex_cn: 老师用简单的词给‘爱’下定义。
words.en: If you define something, you show, describe, or state clearly what it is and what its limits are, or what it is like.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.ex: I will definitely come to the party.
words.ex_cn: 我肯定会来参加派对。
words.en: without any doubt; certainly

words.ex: The dictionary gives a clear definition of the word.
words.ex_cn: 词典给出了这个词的清晰定义。
words.en: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: v. 限制；“confine”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 被限制的；狭窄的；
words.ex: He was confined to his room for a week.
words.ex_cn: 他被限制在房间里一周。
words.en: If something is confined to a particular place, it exists only in that place. If it is confined to a particular group, only the members of that group have it.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: The soldier shoot at the target.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向目标射击。
words.en: To shoot means to fire a bullet from a gun or to take a photograph. It can also refer to the act of a plant sprouting or a player attempting to score in sports by sending the ball or puck towards the goal.

words.tr: v. 射击；拍摄（电影）；疾驰；“shoot”的过去式和过去分词； n. 照片；射击；射门；
words.ex: He shot the target with his gun.
words.ex_cn: 他用枪射击了目标。
words.en: A shot is an act of shooting a gun, or the sound that this makes. It can also refer to an attempt to do something, a photograph, or an injection.

words.tr: n. 射击；发射； v. 射击；射门；疾驰；“shoot”的现在分词；“shoot”的现在分词；
words.ex: Shooting is his favorite sport.
words.ex_cn: 射击是他最喜欢的运动。
words.en: The act of firing a gun or other weapon; the sport of shooting animals or birds for food or sport.

words.tr:
n. 火；
v. 射击；开火；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火在壁炉里熊熊燃烧。
words.en: Fire is the heat and light that comes out when something burns. It can also refer to the act of shooting a weapon or the dismissal of an employee from a job.

words.ex: The company will hire a new manager next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司下周将雇用一位新经理。
words.en: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

words.ex: The company will employ five new workers next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将雇佣五名新员工。
words.en: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

words.ex: The employee arrived at work early.
words.ex_cn: 这位雇员早早到达了工作地点。
words.en: An employee is a person who is paid to work for an organization or for another person.

words.ex: The employer gave her a raise.
words.ex_cn: 雇主给她加了薪。
words.en: An employer is a person or organization that employs people, paying them for their work.

words.ex: He found employment after graduating from university.
words.ex_cn: 他大学毕业后找到了工作。
words.en: the condition of having paid work

words.ex: Many people face unemployment during the economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 在经济危机期间，许多人面临失业。
words.en: Unemployment refers to the state of being without a job, especially when one is actively seeking employment.

words.tr:
v. 吹；打击；
n. 打击；
words.ex: The wind blows the leaves away.
words.ex_cn: 风吹走了树叶。
words.en: To move air or gas forcefully; to strike something with force.

words.ex: The wolf howl at the moon.
words.ex_cn: 狼对着月亮嚎叫。
words.en: If a dog or wolf howls, it makes a long, loud, crying sound. If a person howls, they make a long, loud cry expressing pain, anger, or unhappiness.

words.ex: He blew a whistle to get our attention.
words.ex_cn: 他吹了一声口哨来引起我们的注意。
words.en: A whistle is a small metal tube which you blow in order to produce a loud sound and attract someone's attention. A whistle is also the sound that you make when you blow a whistle or when you whistle.

words.tr:
v. 耳语；低语
n. 耳语；低语；沙沙的声音
words.ex: He whispered a secret to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友低语了一个秘密。
words.en: To speak very quietly using one's breath rather than one's throat, especially for the sake of privacy.

words.tr:
n. 流动；
v. 流动；
words.ex: The flow of water in the river is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 河里水的流动非常快。
words.en: To move along or out steadily and continuously in a current or stream.

words.tr:
n. 旗；旗帜；信号旗；
v. 用旗标记；
words.ex: The flag waves in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: A flag is a piece of cloth with a special design or colors that is used as a symbol, or to give a signal.

words.ex: He will flee from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 他会从着火的房子里逃走。
words.en: If you flee from something or someone, you leave them quickly because you are afraid of them or because you do not want to be involved with them.

words.ex: He speaks fluent English.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一口流利的英语。
words.en: If someone is fluent in a particular language, they can speak it easily and correctly.

words.ex: He speaks English fluently.
words.ex_cn: 他流利地讲英语。
words.en: If you speak a language or read fluently, you speak or read it easily, well, and quickly.

words.ex: He speaks English with great fluency.
words.ex_cn: 他英语说得很流利。
words.en: Fluency is the ability to speak or write a language easily and well.

words.tr:
adj. 平滑的；平坦的；
v. 使平滑；
words.ex: The glass surface is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃表面是平滑的。
words.en: Having an even and regular surface or consistency; free from projections, indentations, or roughness.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.ex: The course of the river changed after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流程在洪水后发生了变化。
words.en: A course is a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject.

words.ex: The wood surface is rough.
words.ex_cn: 木头表面很粗糙。
words.en: If a surface is rough, it is not smooth and has bumps or uneven areas.

words.tr: adj. 艰苦的；强硬的；严厉的；
words.ex: The hike was tough but beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这次徒步旅行很艰苦但很美丽。
words.en: A tough person is strong and determined, and can tolerate difficulty or suffering.

words.ex: He finished the work ahead of time.
words.ex_cn: 他提前完成了工作。
words.en: If someone is ahead in a competition or comparison, they are winning or doing better than the other people involved.

words.ex: There are roughly 100 students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级大约有100名学生。
words.en: In a manner that is not exact or detailed; approximately.

words.ex: He wiped sweat from his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他擦去了额头上的汗水。
words.en: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.tr:
adv. 向前；前进；
v. 促进；转交；
adj. 向前的；前进的；
words.ex: He walked forward to meet the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向前走去见老师。
words.en: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. In British English, you can also say that you are looking forward to something that is going to happen.

words.ex: We ate dinner, and afterward we watched a movie.
words.ex_cn: 我们吃了晚饭，之后看了部电影。
words.en: If you do something or if something happens afterward, you do it or it happens after a particular event or time that has already been mentioned.

words.tr:
adv. 后来；稍后；
adj. 后来的；稍后的；晚些的；晚年的；
words.ex: He left the party, and later he called his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了派对，后来给朋友打了电话。
words.en: Later means after the present time or after the time you are talking about.

words.tr:
n. 后者（the ~）；
adj. 后期的；后面的；
words.ex: I like tea and coffee; I prefer the latter.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢茶和咖啡；我更喜欢后者。
words.en: The latter is used to refer to the second of two things or people mentioned.

words.tr:
adj. 最新的；最后的；最近的；
n. 最新事物；
words.ex: He bought the latest phone on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他买了市场上最新的手机。
words.en: The most recent or the newest.

words.ex: I haven't seen him lately.
words.ex_cn: 我最近没见到他。
words.en: If you say that something has happened lately, you mean that it has happened recently.

words.ex: He is a former teacher who now works as a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名以前的老师，现在是一名作家。
words.en: Former is used to describe someone who used to have a particular job, position, or role, but no longer has it.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.ex: He worked here previously.
words.ex_cn: 他以前在这里工作。
words.en: At an earlier time or before.

words.ex: He visits his grandparents every fortnight.
words.ex_cn: 他每两周拜访一次祖父母。
words.en: A fortnight is a period of two weeks.

words.tr:
adj. 两星期一次的；隔周发行的
adv. 两周一次地
n. 双周刊
words.ex: He gets paid fortnightly.
words.ex_cn: 他每两周领一次工资。
words.en: Fortnightly means happening or appearing once every two weeks.

words.tr:
adv. 向后地；
adj. 向后的；
words.ex: He walked backward to see the sign.
words.ex_cn: 他向后走以便看清楚那个标志。
words.en: If you move or look backward, you move or look in the direction that your back is facing.

words.tr:
adv. 向上地；
adj. 向上的；
words.ex: The balloon moved upward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 气球缓慢地向上移动。
words.en: Moving or directed toward a higher place or level.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The garden has fragrant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有芳香的花。
words.en: Having a pleasant or sweet smell.

words.ex: The flower has a sweet fragrance.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有一种甜美的香味。
words.en: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, especially that of a flower or perfume.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.tr:
n. 毒药；毒物；
v. 毒害；
words.ex: The snake's poison can kill quickly.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒药能迅速致死。
words.en: A poison is a substance that causes harm or death if it is swallowed, absorbed, or breathed in. It can also refer to something that has a very harmful effect on something else.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The framework of the house is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 房子的骨架是木制的。
words.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

words.tr:
n. 火焰
v. 燃烧；爆发；面红
words.ex: The candle flame flickered in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的火焰在风中摇曳。
words.en: A flame is a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is burning.

words.tr: adj. 燃烧的； v. “flame”的现在分词；
words.ex: The flaming torch lit up the night.
words.ex_cn: 燃烧的火炬照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is flaming is burning strongly and producing a lot of flames.

words.ex: She put the ice cream in the freezer.
words.ex_cn: 她把冰淇淋放进冷冻柜里。
words.en: A freezer is a device that is used to store food at very low temperatures in order to preserve it.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.tr: adj. 极冷的；冰冻的； v. 结冰；冻结；“freeze”的现在分词；
words.ex: The weather is freezing today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气极冷。
words.en: If you say that something is freezing, you are emphasizing that it is very cold.

words.ex: There was frost on the grass this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上草地上有霜。
words.en: A thin layer of ice that forms on surfaces when the temperature drops below freezing.

words.ex: The car drove slowly through the fog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车缓缓驶过浓雾。
words.en: Fog is a thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the atmosphere at or near the earth's surface which obscures or restricts visibility (to a greater extent than mist; strictly, reducing visibility to below 1 km).

words.ex: The morning was foggy, so I could not see the road.
words.ex_cn: 早晨有雾，所以我看不到路。
words.en: If it is foggy, there is fog.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.ex: A gentle breeze blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵微风轻轻吹过树梢。
words.en: A breeze is a gentle wind.

words.ex: The gale knocked down several trees.
words.ex_cn: 大风刮倒了几棵树。
words.en: A gale is a very strong wind.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: The brain controls our thoughts and movements.
words.ex_cn: 大脑控制我们的思想和行动。
words.en: The brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

words.ex: He uses a digital watch to tell time.
words.ex_cn: 他用一块数字手表看时间。
words.en: Digital systems, devices, or technology use electronic signals that are represented by the numbers 1 and 0, indicating 'on' or 'off'.

words.ex: He has a mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 他有心理疾病。
words.en: Relating to the mind or involving the process of thinking.

words.tr: adv. 精神上；思想上；智力上；
words.ex: He is mentally strong despite his challenges.
words.ex_cn: 尽管面临挑战，他在精神上很坚强。
words.en: In a manner relating to the mind or mental processes.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.tr:
adj. 总的；全部的；
n. 总计；总额；
v. 共计；总数达；
words.ex: The total cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 总费用是50美元。
words.en: The whole amount or number; the sum total.

words.ex: I totally agree with you.
words.ex_cn: 我完全同意你的观点。
words.en: Used to emphasize that something is completely true or correct.

words.ex: He has a talent for playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他有弹钢琴的才能。
words.en: If someone has a talent for something, they have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: There was silence after the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 坏消息传来后，一片沉默。
words.en: The absence of sound; complete quiet.

words.ex: The children were silent during the movie.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在看电影时很安静。
words.en: Someone or something that is silent makes no noise at all.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.tr: adj. 聪明的；时髦的；衣冠楚楚的；
words.ex: He is a smart student who solves math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个聪明的学生，能快速解决数学问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as smart, you mean that they are clean, tidy, and stylish in their appearance.

words.tr: adj. 充满智慧的；明智的；英明的；
words.ex: The wise old man gave good advice.
words.ex_cn: 这位充满智慧的老人给出了很好的建议。
words.en: If you describe someone as wise, you mean that they have experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

words.ex: His wisdom helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的智慧帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: Wisdom is the ability to use your knowledge and experience to make good decisions and judgments.

words.tr: adv. 否则；在其他方面；除此之外；
words.ex: Hurry up, otherwise you'll be late.
words.ex_cn: 快点，否则你会迟到的。
words.en: in circumstances different from those present or considered; or else

words.ex: It was foolish to walk on the ice.
words.ex_cn: 在冰上走是愚蠢的。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is foolish, you mean that they are not sensible or show a lack of good judgment.

words.ex: He made a stupid mistake on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is stupid, you mean that they show a lack of good judgment or intelligence and they are not at all sensible.

words.ex: His silly hat made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那可笑的帽子让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is silly, you mean that they are foolish, childish, or ridiculous.

words.ex: He sent the message via email.
words.ex_cn: 他通过电子邮件发送了这条消息。
words.en: If you go somewhere via a particular place, you go through that place on the way to your destination.

words.ex: The victim cried for help.
words.ex_cn: 受害者呼救。
words.en: A victim is someone who has been harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event or action.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.ex: The team celebrated their victory after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，球队庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A victory is a success in a struggle, war, or competition.

words.tr:
n. 视频；录像；
adj. 视频的；录像的；
words.ex: I watched a short video on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我看了一个YouTube上的短视频。
words.en: A recording of moving visual images made digitally or on videotape.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.ex: The violent storm destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场暴力的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If someone is violent, or if they do something that is violent, they use physical force or weapons to hurt, injure, or kill other people.

words.ex: The movie shows too much violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了太多的暴力。
words.en: Violence is behavior which is intended to hurt, injure, or kill people.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: The critic praised the new movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位评论家称赞了这部新电影。
words.en: A critic is a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, films, music, etc.

words.ex: He received criticism for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: Criticism is the act of expressing disapproval of someone or something and of the faults they have or the mistakes they have made.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: He primarily works as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他主要是一名老师。
words.en: You use primarily to say what is mainly true in a particular situation.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: The coat is made of soft fur.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套是由柔软的毛皮制成的。
words.en: The thick hair that covers the bodies of some animals, or the hair-covered skin(s) of animals, used in making clothes and other items.

words.tr: v. 布置家具；配备；供给；提供
words.ex: He will furnish the apartment with new furniture.
words.ex_cn: 他将为公寓配备新家具。
words.en: To furnish a place means to put furniture and other things into it.

words.ex: The room has new furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有新家具。
words.en: Furniture refers to the movable objects intended to support various human activities such as seating, eating, and sleeping.

words.tr:
n. 油漆；绘画颜料；
v. 刷油漆；画；
words.ex: The paint on the wall is peeling.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的油漆正在剥落。
words.en: Paint is a coloured liquid that you put onto a surface with a brush in order to protect the surface or to make it look nice, or to produce a picture.

words.tr: n. 绘画；油画； v. 刷油漆；用颜料画；“paint”的现在分词；
words.ex: He loves painting in his free time.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在空闲时间绘画。
words.en: A painting is a picture which someone has painted.

words.ex: The students gathered in the hall for the assembly.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在大厅里集合。
words.en: A hall is a large room or building which is used for public events such as concerts, exhibitions, and meetings.

words.ex: He goes to the mall to buy clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他去商场买衣服。
words.en: A mall is a large enclosed shopping area from which traffic is excluded.

words.tr:
adj. 一般的；普遍的；总的；大致的；首席的；
n. 将军；
words.ex: He gave a general answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个一般的回答。
words.en: A general is a high-ranking officer in the army or air force. In other contexts, general refers to something that is common, usual, or not specific.

words.ex: She generally wakes up at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 她通常在早上七点起床。
words.en: In most cases; usually.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.ex: The team made a smart strategy to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队制定了一项聪明的策略来赢得比赛。
words.en: A strategy is a plan that you use in order to achieve something.

words.ex: He made a strategic decision to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有战略性的决定来省钱。
words.en: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.

words.tr:
pron. 我的（东西）；
n. 矿；
v. 采矿；
words.ex: This book is mine.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是我的。
words.en: Used to refer to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker. A place where minerals are extracted from the earth. To extract minerals from the earth.

words.ex: Rock contains many minerals.
words.ex_cn: 岩石中含有许多矿物。
words.en: A mineral is a solid substance that occurs naturally and has a specific chemical composition and structure.

words.ex: He burns coal to keep his house warm.
words.ex_cn: 他烧煤来让房子暖和。
words.en: Coal is a hard black substance that is extracted from the ground and burned as fuel.

words.ex: The fish swim among the coral in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海中的珊瑚间游动。
words.en: A hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates as an external skeleton, typically forming large reefs in warm seas.

words.tr: adj. 有苦味的；激烈而不快的；痛苦的；刺痛的；
words.ex: The medicine tastes bitter.
words.ex_cn: 这种药尝起来很苦。
words.en: Having a sharp, pungent taste or smell; not sweet. Feeling or showing anger, hurt, or resentment because of bad experiences or a sense of unjust treatment.

words.ex: The wind blew bitterly through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 风刺骨地吹过树林。
words.en: In a way that is filled with or marked by strong negative emotions such as anger, sorrow, or disappointment.

words.tr:
n. 轨道；
v. 绕...轨道而行；
words.ex: The moon moves around the Earth in an orbit.
words.ex_cn: 月亮围绕地球在轨道上运行。
words.en: An orbit is the curved path, usually elliptical, described by a planet, satellite, spaceship, etc., around a celestial body, as the sun.

words.tr:
n. 咬；咬伤；上钩；
v. 咬；叮；上钩；
words.ex: The dog gave him a sudden bite.
words.ex_cn: 狗突然咬了他一口。
words.en: If an animal or person bites you, they use their teeth to cut into your flesh.

words.ex: He put sugar in his tea.
words.ex_cn: 他把糖放进茶里。
words.en: A sweet substance that is used to make food and drinks sweet. It is usually in the form of white or brown crystals.

words.ex: She put honey on her toast.
words.ex_cn: 她在吐司上涂了蜂蜜。
words.en: Honey is a sweet, sticky, yellowish-brown fluid made by bees and other insects from nectar collected from flowers.

words.tr:
adj. 甜的；悦人的；
n. 糖果；
words.ex: The cake is sweet and delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕又甜又美味。
words.en: Sweet is used to describe something that tastes of sugar or is pleasant in a way that is reminiscent of sugar. It can also describe something that is pleasing to the senses other than taste, such as a sound or smell, or something that is kind and gentle.

words.ex: He sweats heavily after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后大量出汗。
words.en: Sweat is the salty liquid that comes out through the skin when you are hot, ill, or afraid.

words.ex: He wears a warm sweater in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿一件暖和的毛衣。
words.en: A sweater is a piece of clothing that you wear on the upper part of your body. It is usually made of wool or cotton and has long sleeves.

words.ex: The soup is too salty.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太咸了。
words.en: Something that is salty contains salt or tastes of salt.

words.ex: The lemon tastes sour.
words.ex_cn: 这个柠檬尝起来是酸的。
words.en: Having a sharp, acidic taste; not sweet.

words.ex: Farmers grow wheat in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植小麦。
words.en: Wheat is a cereal plant that is grown in temperate countries and is the most important kind grown for food.

words.ex: She adds flour to make bread.
words.ex_cn: 她加面粉来做面包。
words.en: Flour is a powder made by grinding raw grains, roots, beans, nuts, or seeds. It is used to make many different foods.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.ex: Farmers grow corn as a crop.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植玉米作为农作物。
words.en: A crop is a plant such as wheat, potatoes, or cotton that is grown in large quantities by farmers.

words.ex: The apple is ripe and ready to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果熟了，可以吃了。
words.en: When fruit or crops are ripe, they are ready to be eaten or harvested because they have developed to the right stage.

words.ex: The apples ripen in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在秋天成熟。
words.en: When crops ripen or when the sun ripens them, they become ripe and ready to eat.

words.tr:
n. 收获；收成；
v. 收获；收割；
words.ex: The farmers celebrated the harvest in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 农民们在秋天庆祝收获。
words.en: The harvest is the process of gathering mature crops from the fields. It is a crucial activity in agriculture that marks the end of the growing season.

words.ex: He worked hard and reaped the rewards.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，获得了回报。
words.en: To reap means to cut and gather a crop, or to obtain something, especially as a result of effort.

words.ex: He left a heap of clothes on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把一堆衣服扔在地上。
words.en: A heap of things is a pile of them, especially a pile arranged in a rather untidy way.

words.tr:
n. 领域；田地；场地；运动场；
v. 处理，应付（问题、电话等）；
words.ex: He works in the field of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机科学领域工作。
words.en: A field is an area of land that is used for a particular purpose, such as growing crops or playing sports.

words.ex: The workers drill for oil in the oilfield.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在油田钻探石油。
words.en: An oilfield is an area of land or sea under which there is oil.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.tr:
v. 生产；制造；导致；引起；生育；出示；
n. 农产品；
words.ex: The farm produces fresh vegetables every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每天生产新鲜蔬菜。
words.en: To produce something means to make, create, or manufacture it, often in large quantities. It can also refer to the act of causing something to happen or exist.

words.ex: Fish reproduce in the river.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在河里繁殖。
words.en: To produce something again; to make a copy of something.

words.ex: This company makes a new product every year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司每年都会推出一种新产品。
words.en: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.

words.ex: The factory increases its production every year.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每年都在增加生产。
words.en: Production refers to the process of manufacturing or growing something in large quantities, or the amount of something that is manufactured or grown.

words.ex: The store sells many kinds of goods.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种商品。
words.en: Goods are items that are made to be sold.

words.ex: The goose is swimming in the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹅正在湖里游泳。
words.en: A goose is a large bird that has a long neck and webbed feet. Geese are often kept for their meat, feathers, or as guard animals.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: He got a teaching qualification last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了教师资格。
words.en: A qualification is a skill or type of experience that you need in order to do a particular job or activity.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.ex: He works in the tech industry.
words.ex_cn: 他在科技行业工作。
words.en: Industry is the work and processes involved in collecting raw materials, and making them into products in factories.

words.ex: The city has many industrial factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市有许多工业工厂。
words.en: Industrial means relating to or characterized by industry.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: He is jealous of his brother's new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒他弟弟的新自行车。
words.en: If someone is jealous, they feel angry or bitter because they think that another person is trying to take a lover or friend, or a possession, away from them.

words.ex: I envy her for her happy family.
words.ex_cn: 我羡慕她幸福的家庭。
words.en: Envy is the feeling you have when you wish you could have the same thing or quality that someone else has.

words.ex: He felt envious when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到嫉妒。
words.en: If you are envious of someone, you want something that they have.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.ex: The maid cleans the house every morning.
words.ex_cn: 女仆每天早上打扫房子。
words.en: A maid is a woman who works as a servant in a hotel or in someone's home.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.tr: adj. 温和的；文雅的；温柔的；
words.ex: The mother gave a gentle hug to her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲给了孩子一个温和的拥抱。
words.en: Someone who is gentle is kind and calm, and does not behave in a violent or harsh way.

words.tr: adv. 温柔地；温和地；轻轻地；
words.ex: She gently woke the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她温柔地叫醒了宝宝。
words.en: In a mild, kind, or tender manner; not harshly or severely.

words.ex: He is polite to everyone he meets.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Having or showing behavior that is respectful and considerate of other people.

words.ex: The savage wolf howled under the moon.
words.ex_cn: 那头野性的狼在月光下嚎叫。
words.en: A savage person or animal is very fierce and violent.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.ex: She took a glance at the clock.
words.ex_cn: 她瞥了一眼钟。
words.en: If you glance at something or someone, you look at them very quickly and then look away again immediately.

words.ex: He carried his baggage to the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他把行李带到了机场。
words.en: Baggage refers to the suitcases and bags that you take with you when you travel, or it can refer to emotional issues that someone carries with them from past experiences.

words.ex: He packed his luggage before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他在旅行前收拾好了行李。
words.en: Luggage consists of the suitcases and bags that you take with you when you travel.

words.ex: The beggar sat on the street with a cup.
words.ex_cn: 那个乞丐坐在街上，手里拿着一个杯子。
words.en: A beggar is a person who lives by asking people for money or food.

words.tr:
n. 一系列；（变化）范围；山脉；
v. （在某范围内）变化；包括（各种不同的人或物）；
words.ex: The store offers a range of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供一系列颜色。
words.en: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind.

words.ex: I will arrange a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天安排一次会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.ex: We made an arrangement to meet at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我们安排好晚上六点见面。
words.en: An arrangement is a plan or preparation which you make so that something can happen.

words.ex: He stared at the moon all night.
words.ex_cn: 他整晚凝视着月亮。
words.en: To look fixedly or intently at someone or something.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: The glare of the sun made it hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 阳光的刺眼使我看不清。
words.en: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face. Glare is also a very bright light that is uncomfortable to look at.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: He scan the QR code with his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机扫描了二维码。
words.en: To look at something carefully or quickly in order to find out specific information or to examine something thoroughly.

words.ex: He uses a scanner to copy documents.
words.ex_cn: 他使用扫描仪来复制文件。
words.en: A scanner is a device that captures images from photographic prints, posters, magazine pages, and similar sources for computer editing and display.

words.ex: The scandal made the news last week.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻上周上了新闻。
words.en: A scandal is a situation or event that is thought to be shocking and immoral and that everyone knows about.

words.ex: The Earth is a globe.
words.ex_cn: 地球是一个球体。
words.en: The globe is the world; especially used to refer to the Earth as a planet.

words.ex: The problem is a global issue.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题是一个全球性的问题。
words.en: relating to the whole world; worldwide

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.tr:
n. 胶；胶水；
v. 粘合；
words.ex: He used glue to stick the paper together.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶把纸粘在一起。
words.en: A sticky substance used for joining things together.

words.ex: He ate gruel for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了稀粥。
words.en: A thin liquid food of oatmeal or other meal boiled in milk or water.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.ex: The golden sun set behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 金色的太阳在山后落下。
words.en: Something that is golden is bright yellow in color, like gold. It can also describe something that is very good or valuable.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.ex: The bridge is made of iron.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥是用铁建造的。
words.en: Iron is a strong hard metal that is used to make steel and is also found in small quantities in blood and food.

words.ex: The bridge is made of steel.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥是用钢建造的。
words.en: Steel is a very strong metal made mainly from iron. It is used for making many things such as bridges, buildings, and vehicles.

words.ex: She wore a beautiful jewel on her finger.
words.ex_cn: 她手指上戴着一颗漂亮的珠宝。
words.en: A jewel is a precious stone that is used to decorate valuable objects such as rings or necklaces.

words.ex: She wore beautiful jewellery to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了漂亮的珠宝去参加派对。
words.en: Jewellery consists of objects that are worn for personal adornment, such as bracelets, rings, necklaces, and earrings, often made from precious metals and gemstones.

words.ex: She wore a diamond ring on her finger.
words.ex_cn: 她手指上戴着一枚钻石戒指。
words.en: A diamond is a precious stone consisting of a clear and colorless crystalline form of pure carbon, the hardest naturally occurring substance.

words.ex: She wears a necklace made of crystal.
words.ex_cn: 她戴一条水晶制成的项链。
words.en: A crystal is a solid that has a regular, repeating arrangement of atoms. Crystals are often transparent and can be used in jewelry or as decorative objects.

words.ex: She wears a silk dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件丝绸连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: A fine, strong, soft, lustrous fiber produced by silkworms in making cocoons and collected to make thread and fabric.

words.ex: He wears a nylon jacket to stay dry.
words.ex_cn: 他穿一件尼龙夹克来保持干燥。
words.en: Nylon is a strong, elastic synthetic fiber used especially in the manufacture of clothing, ropes, and brushes.

words.ex: She knits a sweater from wool.
words.ex_cn: 她用羊毛织毛衣。
words.en: Wool is the hair that grows on sheep and some other animals, which is used to make clothes, blankets, etc.

words.ex: She wore a woollen scarf in winter.
words.ex_cn: 她冬天戴了一条毛纺围巾。
words.en: Made of wool; relating to wool.

words.ex: He apologised for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而道歉了。
words.en: To say that you are sorry for something that you have done, especially something that has caused inconvenience or upset someone.

words.ex: He gave her a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他向她真诚地道歉了。
words.en: An apology is something that you say or write in order to tell someone that you are sorry that you have hurt them or caused trouble for them.

words.tr:
n. 遗憾；
v. 懊悔；
words.ex: He felt a deep regret after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失去工作后感到深深的遗憾。
words.en: If you regret something that you have done, you wish that you had not done it.

words.tr: adj. 后悔的；失望的；令人惋惜的
words.ex: He looked regretful after shouting at his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友大喊后看起来很后悔。
words.en: feeling or expressing regret; sorrowful or sorry

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.ex: He showed gratitude for the help.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了对帮助的感激。
words.en: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful and appreciative.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.ex: He showed appreciation for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的辛勤工作表示欣赏。
words.en: Recognition of the quality, value, significance, or magnitude of people and things.

words.ex: This necklace is precious to her.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链对她来说很珍贵。
words.en: If you say that something such as a resource is precious, you mean that it is valuable and should not be wasted or used badly.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The ancient tomb was filled with artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的坟墓里充满了文物。
words.en: A tomb is a place where a dead person is buried, especially a large, impressive structure.

words.ex: The gravity of Earth pulls objects down.
words.ex_cn: 地球的重力把物体往下拉。
words.en: Gravity is the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth or towards any other physical body having mass.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.tr: v. 伤心；悲痛；使悲痛；使伤心
words.ex: He grieves for his lost dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为失去的狗感到悲痛。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or distress, especially because of someone's death.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.tr: n. 减缓；宽慰；解脱；救济；
words.ex: The medicine brought relief to his pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药缓解了他的疼痛。
words.en: Relief is a feeling of reassurance and relaxation following release from anxiety or distress.

words.ex: His belief in honesty never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对诚实的信念从未改变。
words.en: A belief is a strong feeling that something is true or exists.

words.tr:
adj. 简短的；简明的；短暂的；
v. 为…提供信息；
n. 摘要；概要；
words.ex: He gave a brief answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简短的答案。
words.en: If something is brief, it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: phrase. 简单地说；简而言之；简单扼要地
words.ex: In brief, he likes soccer.
words.ex_cn: 简而言之，他喜欢足球。
words.en: In a few words; concisely.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；认真的；严肃的；
words.ex: The accident caused a serious injury.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故造成了严重的伤害。
words.en: If you are serious about something, you are sincere about it and mean what you say.

words.ex: He watched the whole series of the show.
words.ex_cn: 他看完了这部剧的整个系列。
words.en: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with cancer last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有癌症。
words.en: Cancer is a serious disease caused by cells that are not normal and that can spread to other parts of the body.

words.ex: He felt deep sorrow when his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 当他的狗去世时，他感到深深的悲痛。
words.en: Sorrow is a feeling of deep sadness or regret.

words.tr: adj. 悲伤的；使人伤心的
words.ex: He looked sorrowful after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他看起来很悲伤。
words.en: Feeling or showing sadness; mournful.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 呜咽；抽噎
n. 抽噎（声）；啜泣（声）
words.ex: The little girl sobbed after losing her toy.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在丢失玩具后哭了起来。
words.en: To cry noisily, taking in short breaths.

words.ex: They bury the dead in the cemetery.
words.ex_cn: 他们把死者埋葬在墓地里。
words.en: To bury something means to put it into a hole in the ground and cover it up, often in order to hide it or to put it to rest.

words.ex: The burial took place at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 埋葬在日出时进行。
words.en: The act or ceremony of putting a dead body into a grave.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.tr: n. 奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；
words.ex: She bought a luxury dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件奢华的裙子。
words.en: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

words.ex: He is greedy and always wants more candy.
words.ex_cn: 他很贪婪，总是想要更多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe someone as greedy, you mean that they want to have more of something such as food or money than is necessary or fair.

words.ex: He greet his friend with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着向朋友问好。
words.en: To greet someone means to say hello to them or to welcome them.

words.tr:
n. 问候；迎接；致意
v. 问候；打招呼；迎接；“greet”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave me a warm greeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我一个热情的问候。
words.en: A greeting is something friendly that you say or do when you meet someone.

words.tr:
n. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
v. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
words.ex: The soldier gave a salute to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向军官敬礼。
words.en: If you salute someone, you greet them or show your respect with a formal sign. Soldiers usually salute officers by raising their right hand so that their fingers touch their forehead.

words.ex: He insured his car against accidents.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的车投保了意外险。
words.en: If you insure yourself or your property, you pay money to an insurance company so that if you become ill or if your property is damaged or stolen, the company will pay you a sum of money.

words.ex: He bought insurance for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了保险。
words.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay money to you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

words.ex: Please ensure the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 请确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make certain that something will occur or be the case.

words.ex: I assure you that everything will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 我向你保证一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you assure someone that something is true or will happen, you tell them that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, often in order to make them less worried.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr:
n. 保卫；警卫；
v. 守卫；
words.ex: The guard stands at the gate to protect the building.
words.ex_cn: 保卫人员站在门口保护大楼。
words.en: A guard is a person who protects a place, person, or thing, or who prevents people from escaping from a place.

words.tr:
v. 看待；有关；
n. 尊敬；致意；
words.ex: I regard him as a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 我把他看作好朋友。
words.en: If you regard someone or something as being a particular thing or as having a particular quality, you believe that they are that thing or have that quality.

words.ex: He went outside regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨就出去了。
words.en: If you say that someone does something regardless, you mean that they do it without taking account of the possible problems or difficulties.

words.tr:
n. 担忧；关注；
v. 涉及；
words.ex: His main concern is his child's safety.
words.ex_cn: 他主要的担忧是孩子的安全。
words.en: If something concerns you, it worries you or causes you to feel anxious.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. “concern”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book is concerning climate change.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于气候变化的。
words.en: If something is concerning, it causes you to feel concerned about it.

words.tr:
n. 锤子；
v. 锤打；
words.ex: He hit the nail with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子敲钉子。
words.en: A hammer is a tool that consists of a heavy piece of metal at the end of a handle, used for hitting things.

words.ex: A handful of students stayed after class to ask questions.
words.ex_cn: 少数学生课后留下来提问。
words.en: A handful of something is a small amount of it, especially when it is not enough or when it is difficult to manage.

words.ex: He will hand over the keys tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会交出钥匙。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially because you have been ordered to do so or because it is necessary.

words.ex: He pulled out a handkerchief to wipe his sweat.
words.ex_cn: 他掏出一块手帕擦汗。
words.en: A handkerchief is a small square piece of fabric which you use for blowing your nose.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；首要的；
n. 领袖；首领；
words.ex: He is the chief reason for the team's success.
words.ex_cn: 他是球队成功的主要原因。
words.en: The chief is the leader of a group or organization, or the main part of something.

words.ex: The chef cooked a delicious dinner for the guests.
words.ex_cn: 主厨为客人做了一顿美味的晚餐。
words.en: A chef is a professional cook, typically the chief cook in a restaurant or hotel.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.ex: His handwriting is very neat.
words.ex_cn: 他的笔迹非常工整。
words.en: Handwriting is the style of writing that someone uses when they write with a pen or pencil.

words.ex: A pocket calculator is handy for math problems.
words.ex_cn: 便携式计算器对于数学问题很方便。
words.en: If something is handy, it is useful and easy to use or to reach.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
n. 荫；阴影；
v. 遮蔽；
words.ex: The tree provides shade on a hot day.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在炎热的日子提供荫凉。
words.en: Shade is an area where there is no direct sunlight, or something that provides protection from the sun. It can also refer to a slight difference in color, or to gradually change from one color or tone to another.

words.tr: adj. 破旧的；肮脏破烂的；衣衫褴褛的
words.ex: He wore a shabby coat to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件破旧的外套去学校。
words.en: If you describe something as shabby, you mean that it looks old and is in poor condition.

words.ex: Many children suffer from poverty in poor countries.
words.ex_cn: 许多孩子在贫穷国家遭受贫困。
words.en: Poverty is the state of being extremely poor.

words.tr:
n. 窝；鸟巢；
v. 筑巢；
words.ex: The bird built a nest in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在树上筑了一个窝。
words.en: A nest is a structure made by a bird for laying eggs and sheltering its young. It can also refer to a place where insects or other animals lay eggs or raise their young. As a verb, to nest means to build or use a nest.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；努力工作的
words.ex: He is hard-working and always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他很勤奋，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is hard-working always puts a lot of effort and care into their work.

words.ex: He is lazy and doesn't like to do homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，不喜欢做作业。
words.en: If someone is lazy, they are not willing to work or use any effort to do something.

words.ex: He faced many hardships during the war.
words.ex_cn: 他在战争期间经历了许多困苦。
words.en: Hardship refers to a situation that is difficult to endure because of lack of money, resources, or other basic necessities.

words.tr:
n. 伤害；损害；
v. 伤害；损害；
words.ex: The storm caused great harm to the crops.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对庄稼造成了很大伤害。
words.en: To harm someone or something means to cause them physical injury or to damage them in some other way.

words.ex: The small spider is harmless.
words.ex_cn: 这只小蜘蛛是无害的。
words.en: If someone or something is harmless, they are not dangerous and do not cause any harm.

words.ex: Smoking is harmful to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is harmful has a bad effect on something else, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: The team works in harmony.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队合作得很和谐。
words.en: Harmony is the pleasant combination of different notes of music played at the same time. It can also refer to a situation in which people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when things seem right or suitable together.

words.ex: The team worked in a harmonious way.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以和谐的方式合作。
words.en: A harmonious situation, relationship, or agreement is one in which people are friendly and helpful to one another, and in which there is no serious disagreement or argument.

words.ex: I hate waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: To hate someone or something means to feel intense or passionate dislike for them.

words.tr:
n. 喜爱；赞同；
v. 赞成；偏爱；有利于；
words.ex: He has a favour for chocolate ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 他特别喜欢巧克力冰淇淋。
words.en: If you regard something or someone with favour, you like or support them.

words.tr:
adj. 特别受喜爱的；
n. 特别喜爱的事物；
words.ex: Chocolate is my favourite dessert.
words.ex_cn: 巧克力是我最喜爱的甜点。
words.en: Something or someone that is preferred above all others.

words.ex: He reads books as a hobby.
words.ex_cn: 他读书作为一种爱好。
words.en: A hobby is an activity that you enjoy doing in your spare time.

words.ex: He visits the dentist every six months.
words.ex_cn: 他每六个月去看一次牙医。
words.en: A dentist is a person who is qualified to treat diseases and conditions that affect the teeth and gums, especially the repair and extraction of teeth and the insertion of artificial ones.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: He showed his identity card to enter the building.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了身份证以进入大楼。
words.en: Your identity is who you are, or the qualities of a person or group that make them different from others.

words.ex: I recognised my old friend at the station.
words.ex_cn: 我在车站认出了我的老朋友。
words.en: to know someone or something because you have seen or heard him or her or experienced it before

words.ex: The police used fingerprint identification to find the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用指纹识别来找到嫌疑人。
words.en: Identification is the act of recognizing and naming someone or something, or the process of proving who or what someone or something is.

words.ex: The two shirts are identical.
words.ex_cn: 这两件衬衫是一样的。
words.en: Exactly the same, or very similar.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.tr: n. 图像；形象；画面；影像；
words.ex: The photo shows a clear image of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片展示了山脉的清晰图像。
words.en: An image is a picture that you have in your mind, especially about what someone or something is like or the way they look.

words.ex: Can you imagine a world without phones?
words.ex_cn: 你能想象一个没有电话的世界吗？
words.en: To imagine means to form a mental image or concept of something that is not present or real.

words.ex: Children have a strong imagination.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们有很强的想象力。
words.en: The ability to form pictures or ideas in your mind of things that are new and exciting, or not real.

words.tr:
adj. 道德的；道义上的；
n. 寓意；
words.ex: It is a moral duty to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 说实话是一种道德责任。
words.en: Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.

words.ex: He always follows his morality in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他日常生活中总是遵循自己的道德。
words.en: Morality is the belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable and that other behaviour is wrong.

words.ex: He gave an oral report in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上做了口头报告。
words.en: Relating to the mouth; spoken rather than written.

words.tr: adj. 口头的；口语的； v. 讲话；发言；“speak”的过去分词；
words.ex: He gave a spoken presentation instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他做了口头报告，而不是书面报告。
words.en: relating to speech; using speech rather than writing

words.tr: adj. 直言无讳的；坦率的；
words.ex: He is an outspoken teacher who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位直言不讳的老师，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is outspoken expresses their opinions frankly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The spokeswoman spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 女发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokeswoman is a woman who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization.

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr:
adj. 平静的；镇静的；
v. （使）平静；（使）镇定；
n. 平静；
words.ex: The lake was calm in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很平静。
words.en: If someone is calm, they are not excited, anxious, or upset, but are rational and composed.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: She eats a moon cake during the Mid-Autumn Festival.
words.ex_cn: 她在中秋节吃月饼。
words.en: A traditional Chinese pastry eaten during the Mid-Autumn Festival, typically round in shape to symbolize the full moon.

words.ex: He had a mop of curly hair that always looked messy.
words.ex_cn: 他有一头乱蓬蓬的卷发，总是看起来很凌乱。
words.en: A mop is a tool for cleaning floors, consisting of a bundle of thick strings or a sponge attached to a long handle. As a verb, it means to clean or wipe something with a mop.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr: adj. 即刻的；立即的；紧接的；最近的；
words.ex: He needs immediate help.
words.ex_cn: 他需要即刻的帮助。
words.en: An immediate action, event, or situation happens or exists without any delay.

words.ex: He left the room immediately after the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 铃声一响，他就立即离开了房间。
words.en: If something happens immediately, it happens without any delay.

words.ex: They want to immigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他们想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.ex: Immigration to this country has increased recently.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的移民数量最近增加了。
words.en: Immigration is the act of coming to live permanently in a country that is not your own.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.tr:
n. 海港；
v. 庇护；窝藏；
words.ex: The ship docked at the harbour at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 船在日落时停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbour is an area of water next to the coast where ships and boats can shelter.

words.tr:
n. 进口；重要性；
v. 进口；
words.ex: The country increased its import of oil last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家增加了石油的进口。
words.en: To bring in (goods or services) from a foreign country for sale or use.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the port at noon.
words.ex_cn: 船在中午到达了港口。
words.en: A port is a place where ships load and unload goods or passengers.

words.tr:
n. 输出；出口；
v. 输出；出口；
words.ex: This country is a big export of wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家是小麦的大输出国。
words.en: To send goods to another country for sale.

words.ex: This portable charger works well on trips.
words.ex_cn: 这个便携式充电器在旅行时很好用。
words.en: Capable of being carried or moved about with ease.

words.ex: The porter carried his bags to the taxi.
words.ex_cn: 行李搬运工把他的行李搬到了出租车上。
words.en: A porter is a person whose job is to carry things, especially travelers' luggage at places such as railway stations or hotels.

words.tr:
v. 支持；支撑；
n. 拥护；帮助；
words.ex: My friends support me when I feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 当我感到难过时，我的朋友们支持我。
words.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

words.ex: He showed his passport at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场出示了他的护照。
words.en: A passport is an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country and gives you the right to travel to and from that country.

words.ex: He needs a visa to travel to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 他需要一张签证去日本旅行。
words.en: A visa is an official document, or a stamp put in your passport, which allows you to enter or leave a particular country.

words.tr: n. 通过；通道；段落；短文；
words.ex: The passage of the train through the tunnel was quick.
words.ex_cn: 火车通过隧道的速度很快。
words.en: A passage is a long narrow space with walls or fences on both sides, which connects one place or room with another.

words.ex: A passer-by helped the old man cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 一位路人帮老人过马路。
words.en: A passer-by is a person who is walking past something, especially when something unusual is happening.

words.ex: The passenger got off the bus at the next stop.
words.ex_cn: 这位旅客在下一站下了车。
words.en: A passenger is a person who is traveling in a vehicle but is not the driver or one of the people who works on it.

words.ex: We arrived at the airport early.
words.ex_cn: 我们早早到达了机场。
words.en: An airport is a place where aircraft regularly take off and land, with buildings for passengers to wait in.

words.ex: The aircraft landed safely at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这架航空器在机场安全着陆。
words.en: An aircraft is a vehicle which can fly, for example an aeroplane or a helicopter.

words.ex: The aeroplane flies high in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在高空中飞行。
words.en: An aeroplane is a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that enable it to fly through the air.

words.ex: The helicopter flew over the city.
words.ex_cn: 直升机飞过了城市。
words.en: A helicopter is a type of aircraft that derives both lift and propulsion from one or more sets of horizontally revolving overhead rotors. It is capable of moving vertically and horizontally, the direction of motion being controlled by the pitch of the rotor blades.

words.ex: The jet flew high above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 喷气式飞机在云层上方飞行。
words.en: A jet is an aircraft that is powered by jet engines, allowing it to fly at high speeds. It can also refer to a stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening, or to travel by jet aircraft.

words.ex: The airline lost my luggage.
words.ex_cn: 这家航空公司弄丢了我的行李。
words.en: An airline is a company that provides regular flights to take passengers and goods to different places.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: His smile left a good impression on me.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑给我留下了好印象。
words.en: An idea, feeling, or opinion about something or someone, especially one formed without conscious thought or on the basis of little evidence.

words.tr:
v. 表达；表示；
adj. 明确的；
n. 特快列车；快件服务；
words.ex: He can express his feelings clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的感受。
words.en: If you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

words.ex: His expression showed he was happy.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情显示他很快乐。
words.en: The act of making your thoughts, feelings, etc., known by speech, writing, or some other method.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.tr: adj. 抑郁的； v. 降低；“depress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt depressed after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到抑郁。
words.en: If you are depressed, you are sad and feel that you cannot enjoy anything, because your situation is so difficult and unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 令人抑郁的；令人沮丧的；令人消沉的； v. “depress”的现在分词；
words.ex: The rainy weather made the day feel depressing.
words.ex_cn: 阴雨的天气让这一天感觉令人抑郁。
words.en: Making someone feel very unhappy and without hope.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.ex: The exam was stressful for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这次考试对所有学生来说压力很大。
words.en: If a situation or experience is stressful, it makes you feel worried and tense because of difficulties or problems.

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.tr:
v. 增加；增多；
n. 增加；增长；
words.ex: The company increased its profits last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年增加了利润。
words.en: To increase something means to make it larger in size, amount, or degree.

words.tr:
n. 减少；
v. 减少；降低；
words.ex: There was a decrease in rainfall last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月降雨量减少了。
words.en: If something decreases or you decrease it, it becomes less in quantity, size, or intensity.

words.tr:
v. 落下；掉下；
n. 滴；下落；
words.ex: The apple dropped from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上落了下来。
words.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: phrase. 在衰退中；在下降；在衰落
words.ex: The number of students is in decline.
words.ex_cn: 学生人数正在减少。
words.en: Decreasing in quality, importance, or strength.

words.ex: The road inclines sharply to the top of the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这条路陡峭地倾斜向山顶。
words.en: If you incline to a particular opinion, you have a tendency to think or behave in a particular way.

words.ex: We need to reduce waste in our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

words.ex: The reduction in cost helped the company save money.
words.ex_cn: 成本的减少帮助公司节省了资金。
words.en: The act of making something smaller in size, amount, degree, importance, etc., or the result of this.

words.tr:
v. 举起；提起；抬起；
n. 电梯；搭便车；
words.ex: He lift the box with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用双手举起箱子。
words.en: To lift something means to move it to a higher position. A lift is a device that carries people or goods up and down inside buildings.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: He took the elevator to the 10th floor.
words.ex_cn: 他乘电梯上了十楼。
words.en: An elevator is a device that moves people or goods up and down inside a building.

words.tr:
n. 上升；提高；
v. 上升；提高；
words.ex: There was a rise in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度上升了。
words.en: If an amount or level rises, it increases; if something rises, it moves upwards; if you rise, you stand up; if you rise, you get out of bed.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.tr: v. 增加；引起；筹募；提起；养育；
words.ex: The company will raise wages next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将提高工资。
words.en: To raise something means to move it to a higher position or to increase it in amount or level.

words.ex: Children depend on their parents for food and shelter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们依靠父母提供食物和住所。
words.en: If you say that one thing depends on another, you mean that the first thing will be affected or determined by the second.

words.ex: He lives independently and makes his own decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他独立生活，并自己做决定。
words.en: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so that the first one is not affected or influenced by the second.

words.ex: The country gained independence in 1960.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在1960年获得了独立。
words.en: Independence is the freedom from control or influence of others, allowing one to make decisions and act on one's own.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.tr: n. 悬浮；暂时停职（停学、停赛）；
words.ex: The suspension of dust in the air made the sky look gray.
words.ex_cn: 空气中的尘埃悬浮使天空看起来灰蒙蒙的。
words.en: The act of temporarily stopping something from happening or being in effect, or the state of being stopped in this way.

words.ex: The rain ceased after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，雨停了。
words.en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.

words.tr:
v. 悬挂；吊；
n. 悬挂；
words.ex: He hangs a picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把一幅画挂在墙上。
words.en: To hang something means to attach it to something else so that it is supported from above and does not touch the ground.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 闲逛；徘徊；无所事事地待着
words.ex: They like to hang about after school.
words.ex_cn: 他们喜欢放学后闲逛。
words.en: To spend time somewhere without any real purpose or activity.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 犹豫不前；退缩；踌躇
words.ex: He hung back when the teacher asked a question.
words.ex_cn: 老师提问时，他退后了。
words.en: To hesitate or hold back from taking action, often due to shyness or caution.

words.tr:
n. 暂停；停顿；
v. 暂停；停顿；
words.ex: There was a short pause before he answered.
words.ex_cn: 他回答之前停顿了一下。
words.en: To pause means to stop what you are doing for a short time before continuing.

words.tr: adj. 纯的；纯净的；纯粹的；
words.ex: She drank pure water from the spring.
words.ex_cn: 她喝了从泉水中取的纯净水。
words.en: Something that is pure is clean and does not contain any harmful substances.

words.tr:
adj. 紫色的；
n. 紫色；
words.ex: The flower is purple.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花是紫色的。
words.en: Purple is a color that is a mixture of red and blue.

words.ex: He is selfish and never shares his toys.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，从不分享他的玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is selfish, you mean that they only care about their own interests and do not consider the needs or feelings of other people.

words.tr:
n. 种类；
adj. 善良的；和蔼的；
words.ex: There are many kinds of fruits in the market.
words.ex_cn: 市场上有各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you describe someone as kind, you mean that they are gentle, caring, and helpful.

words.ex: She is kind-hearted and helps her neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 她心地善良，总是帮助邻居。
words.en: If you describe someone as kind-hearted, you mean that they are kind, caring, and generous.

words.ex: He goes to kindergarten every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上幼儿园。
words.en: A kindergarten is a school or class for young children, usually between the ages of four and six.

words.ex: The boy is flying a kite in the park.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在公园里放风筝。
words.en: A kite is a toy consisting of a light frame covered with paper, cloth, or plastic, which you fly in the air at the end of one or more long strings. It is also a bird of prey with long pointed wings and a forked tail.

words.ex: Goodness, I didn't expect to see you here!
words.ex_cn: 天哪，我没料到会在这里见到你！
words.en: Goodness is the quality of being kind, helpful, and honest.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: The child's innocence showed in his honest smile.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的无罪体现在他诚实的微笑中。
words.en: the state or quality of being innocent, especially freedom from sin, moral wrong, or guilt through lack of knowledge of evil

words.ex: He felt guilty for lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对朋友撒谎而感到有罪。
words.en: If you feel guilty, you feel unhappy because you believe that you have done something wrong or have failed to do something which you should have done.

words.ex: This sentence is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个句子很容易理解。
words.en: A sentence is a group of words which, when they are written down, begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark. Most sentences contain a subject and a verb.

words.ex: The police caught the man for a serious crime.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了那个犯下严重罪行的人。
words.en: A crime is an illegal action or activity for which a person can be punished by law.

words.tr:
adj. 犯罪的；
n. 罪犯；
words.ex: He made a criminal mistake by stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了一个犯罪的错误。
words.en: A criminal is a person who has committed a crime.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.ex: The murder happened last night in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这起谋杀发生在昨晚的公园里。
words.en: Murder is the unlawful premeditated killing of one human being by another.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
